definition: AA Coffee Grading refers to a size-based classification system for green coffee beans, primarily used in Kenya and other East African countries. The “AA” designation means beans of the largest size category, typically 7.2mm or larger in diameter . This grading method sorts beans through screens with specific-sized holes, with larger beans generally associated with higher quality. In Kenya’s grading hierarchy, AA represents the premium classification, followed by grades like AB, PB ( peaberry ), and others .

Acrid Coffee Taste refers to a specific and undesirable flavor defect in coffee. It has a harsh, sharp, and irritating quality, which is characteristic of a burning or pungent bitterness. This flaw is distinct from desirable acidity and indicates problems that can range from production and roasting to the brewing process itself.
The AeroPress is a portable, versatile coffee brewer that uses air pressure to push hot water through coffee grounds, producing a concentrated, smooth cup in under two minutes.

The Aerobie coffee maker is a manual brewing device that uses air pressure to extract coffee. It involves steeping ground coffee in hot water before using a plunger to force the liquid through a filter. The device consists of a cylindrical chamber, a plunger, and paper filters that remove sediment while allowing oils to pass through.

Affogato, from the Italian word meaning “drowned,” is a classic Italian dessert-beverage hybrid that consists of a scoop of vanilla gelato or ice cream over which a shot of hot espresso is poured . This elegant creation occupies a unique position in coffee culture , straddling the line between dessert and coffee drink .

Definition and Common Usage After Dinner Roast refers to a dark roast coffee made for consumption after meals. This roast style undergoes extended heating at temperatures between 370°F–540°F during the Maillard reaction, resulting in beans with a bold, rich flavor profile . The intense roasting process reduces caffeine content somewhat compared to lighter roasts—a typical dark roast contains approximately 51 mg of caffeine per serving versus 60 mg in light roasts .

Aftertaste in Coffee (also known as the finish ) refers to the lingering sensory impression of flavor , aroma, and mouthfeel that remains after swallowing. It has a role in indicating coffee quality and brewing precision. This final impression can evolve, revealing deeper notes that are characteristic of the bean’s origin, processing method, and roast level.

Aftertastes—the lingering flavors and mouthfeel sensations post-sip—form coffee’s final impression, bridging initial taste to lasting memory. These residual notes, spanning sweet to ashy, emerge from bean origin, roast, and extraction. Crucially, they expose what first sips may conceal: roast flaws, fading freshness, or brewing missteps.

Aged Coffee refers to coffee produced by storing green, unroasted beans for an extended period, which can range from two to three years to much longer. This process requires controlled conditions and is distinct from coffee that is stale or poorly stored. The managed storage helps develop a specific flavor profile. The resulting brew has earthy and pungent flavors, lower acidity , and increased body .

Ageing, spelled as “aging” in American English, is the gradual accumulation of changes in an individual over the course of their life. In humans, this is a complex, multidimensional journey involving physical, psychological, and social transformation.

An air roaster, also known as a fluid bed roaster, is a coffee roasting machine that uses hot air as the primary heat transfer medium to roast coffee beans. The core principle involves suspending green coffee beans in a stream of heated air, creating a “fluid bed” where beans float and tumble continuously during the roasting process .

Alan Adler is an American inventor. His inventions include aerodynamic toys, such as footballs with fins and flying rings and discs. His Aerobie Pro flying ring set several world records for the farthest thrown object. In 2005 he invented a coffee brewing device and method called the AeroPress . He has approximately 40 patents in electronics, optics, and aerodynamics.

Alkaline Taste in Coffee is a sensory term in coffee tasting describing a dry, chalky, or soapy sensation, distinct from true acidity or bitterness, primarily perceived at the back of the tongue. It is a key characteristic of many dark-roasted coffees and beans from specific regions like Indonesia. Despite the name, coffee is chemically acidic, with this taste arising from minerals and roasting byproducts.

Altura Coffee (from the Spanish word for ‘height’) refers to a designation for coffee beans cultivated at high altitudes, typically above 1,200 meters (4,000 feet). This term is a quality marker for high-grown, often mountain-grown, coffee. It means beans that have matured slowly in cooler temperatures, a process that produces greater density and a more complex flavor profile.

Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by memory loss, cognitive decline, and behavioral changes, primarily associated with the accumulation of amyloid-beta plaques and tau protein tangles in the brain. In some cases, early signs can appear as early as the mid-40s.

American Roast refers to a medium-level roast on the coffee spectrum, between lighter roasts (such as Cinnamon or Light) and darker varieties (like French or Italian) . This roast level has beans with a rich brown color and lacks the oily surface seen in darker roasts . American Roast strikes a balance in flavor, preserving some of the bean’s original characteristics while developing deeper caramelized notes.

Antestia bugs (Antestiopsis spp.), also known as variegated coffee bugs or shield bugs, are small insects belonging to the Pentatomidae family that feed on coffee plants. These pests pierce coffee cherries and beans with their mouthparts, causing physical damage and introducing harmful bacteria into the fruit . The bacteria produce 2-isopropyl-3-methoxypyrazine (IMP) when beans are heated at high temperature , resulting in the distinctive potato taste defect (PTD) .

Arabian Mocha Coffee refers to a premium single-origin coffee variety cultivated in Yemen’s mountainous regions across the Arabian Peninsula . This coffee has a medium to full body with bright acidity and a complex sensory profile . The beans undergo dry processing, where they ferment inside the fruit, developing their signature taste characteristics . The resulting cup has a rich, wine-like flavor with distinctive chocolatey undertones .

Arabic coffee is a general name that refers to the two main ways coffee is prepared in many Arab countries: Turkish-style, and Saudi Coffee. The Turkish coffee brewing method is common in the Levant, but brewed without the addition of sugar. Cardamom is often added, or it is served plain قهوة سادة qahwah sādah (lit. “plain coffee”).

Artisan Coffee refers to coffee produced through a hands-on, craftsmanship-focused process. This approach is known for small-batch roasting , direct relationships with farmers, and meticulous attention to quality from cultivation to brewing . It is a type of production within the specialty coffee movement, distinguished by its philosophy and production scale.

Arusha coffee takes its name from the Arusha region in northern Tanzania, where this Arabica variety has been cultivated since the colonial period. The variety emerged from French Mission Bourbon stock introduced to the area in the early 20th century, adapting to the volcanic soils and high-altitude conditions surrounding Mount Meru and Mount Kilimanjaro.

Ashy Coffee Definition and Sensory Profile Ashy coffee refers to beans with a burnt character reminiscent of cigarette ash or fireplace remnants. This negative flavor attribute results from excessive roasting , particularly when beans remain in a drum roaster beyond approximately 17 minutes, leading to burnt or baked flavors . The ashy profile has a dry, powdery sensation on the palate, often accompanied by bitter , charcoal-like notes that overwhelm the coffee’s inherent qualities.

A civet is a small, slender mammal, most active at night, that inhabits the tropical forests of Asia and Africa. The term refers to over a dozen distinct species, with the greatest variety found in Southeast Asia. The most well-known of these is the African Civet, or *Civettictis civetta*. Historically, this animal was the main source of a powerful musky substance used in the creation of fine perfumes, giving it significant economic importance for centuries.

Aspiration in Coffee Tasting refers to a standardized sensory evaluation technique. It involves a taster drawing brewed coffee into the mouth through vigorous, audible suction. The technique is a core component of professional coffee cupping protocols. This method atomizes the liquid to coat the tongue evenly and releases aromatic vapors for retronasal olfaction.

Astringency in coffee describes a tactile sensation rather than a taste, characterized by a dry, puckering feeling in the mouth similar to the experience of over-extracted espresso or strong black tea . This sensation occurs when compounds in the brew bind with proteins in saliva, reducing lubrication and creating a rough, sometimes chalky mouthfeel . While mild astringency can add complexity to a coffee’s sensory profile, excessive astringency is generally considered a defect in the cup.

Australia , officially the Commonwealth of Australia, is a country comprising the mainland of the Australian continent, the island of Tasmania and numerous smaller islands. It is the world’s sixth-largest country by total area. Neighbouring countries include Indonesia , East Timor and Papua New Guinea to the north; the Solomon Islands, Vanuatu and New Caledonia to the north-east; and New Zealand to the south-east.

Baggy Coffee refers to a traditional brewing method where coffee grounds are placed in a cup, then saturated with hot water and left to steep. After approximately 4 minutes, the grounds sink to the bottom . The coffee becomes drinkable between 5-15 minutes after the initial break, allowing time for flavors to develop while the temperature drops to a comfortable drinking range .

Baked Coffee A roasting defect characterized by flat, dull flavor profiles lacking complexity and vibrancy. Baked coffee results from insufficient heat application during the development phase after first crack . The sensory profile has distinctly underwhelming characteristics: muted acidity , diminished sweetness, and a generic caramelized taste that lacks distinction . When cupped, baked coffees often show a papery mouthfeel with minimal aromatic qualities.

Balance in coffee refers to a harmonious and pleasing equilibrium where no single attribute—acidity, sweetness, bitterness , body, or flavor—dominates over the others. This concept is one of the sought-after qualities in specialty coffee , distinguishing exceptional cups from good ones. A balanced coffee is not neutral; it can be complex and vibrant, but its elements are integrated and none are jarring or out of place.

Many coffee machines use pressure to enhance brewing parameters. Some of the devices that use pressure are single serve coffee machines , such as Keurig, or Tassimo, and espresso machines . Other devices are the Moka pot , or steam espresso makers. Pressure is measured in bar.
A barista is a trained coffee professional who specializes in preparing and serving espresso-based drinks, with expertise in extraction, milk texturing, and latte art.

The main piece of a French press is a glass beaker. Because the beaker is exposed to high temperatures in a short time, they are subject to thermal shock , This is why beakers for French press coffee makers are made of borosilicate glass , or more recently, of stainless steel .

A bean hopper is the compartment atop a coffee grinder that stores whole coffee beans before grinding. Made from plastic, metal, or glass, it protects beans from light, air, and moisture—factors that harm freshness and flavor. Its design controls bean flow into the grinder’s burrs, ensuring even grind size for consistent extraction .

Beko is a domestic appliance and consumer electronics brand of Arçelik A. Ş.. Beko Elektronik A. Ş. (later Grundig Elektronik A. Ş. ) was a Turkish consumer electronics manufacturer, owned by Arçelik. In 2004 Beko Elektronik purchased Grundig and by January 2005, Beko and its rival Turkish electronics and white goods brand Vestel accounted for more than half of all TV sets manufactured in Europe. In April 2008 Beko renamed itself Grundig Elektronik A. Ş.

A Bialetti is an Italian brand synonymous with the Moka Express, a stovetop coffee maker invented by Alfonso Bialetti in 1933. It has a distinctive octagonal aluminum body and brews espresso-like coffee by forcing steam-pressurized water through ground coffee. Its affordability and simplicity democratized café-style brewing, establishing it as a global household staple.

Invented in 1933 by Alfonso Bialetti, the Bialetti Moka Express is a stovetop coffee maker that uses steam pressure to make espresso-like coffee. Its three-chamber design—a water-filled base, a middle funnel for ground coffee, and a top collector for the brew—relies on a pressure-driven mechanism. When heated, steam pushes water through the grounds, creating a rich, concentrated coffee.

Bica (pronounced BEE-kah) refers to Portugal ’s standard espresso -style coffee. It is a small, strong shot served in a demitasse cup and is known for being the default coffee ordered nationwide. The term is often used interchangeably with um café (a coffee). As a type of espresso variation, it involves extracting a larger volume of water, which produces a smoother taste . This characteristic flavor profile is linked to Portugal’s tradition of lighter coffee roasting .

Bicerin (pronounced bee-cheh-REEN) is a traditional layered coffee beverage from Turin, Italy. Its name derives from the Piedmontese word for ‘small glass’. The drink is a specific type of coffee-chocolate preparation, celebrated for its three distinct, un-stirred layers.

Bisphenol A (BPA) is an organic compound with the chemical formula (CH3)2C(C6H4OH)2. It is a key building block for making clear, strong plastics and epoxy resins. First used commercially in 1957, its global production now reaches about 3.6 million tons every year. This BPA-based plastic is found in many everyday items, including water bottles, sports gear, and digital media like CDs. In industry, it has a crucial role in lining water pipes to prevent corrosion and coating the insides of many food and beverage cans, forming a protective barrier.

Bitterness represents one of the five basic tastes that the human palate can detect, with receptors concentrated primarily at the back of the tongue. In coffee, this fundamental taste sensation results from the extraction of specific compounds, particularly caffeine and certain phenolic acids. The primary chemical contributors to coffee’s bitter profile are caffeine and chlorogenic acid lactones, which develop during the roasting process .
Black & Decker has a division of domestic coffee maker appliances. The division focuses on the auto drip coffee makers as the most popular coffee brewing method .

A Black Eye is a coffee drink composed of a standard drip coffee (typically 8-12 oz) with a double shot of espresso added to it . The double shot of espresso contributes approximately 60mL of concentrated coffee, enhancing both the caffeine content and flavor profile . While caffeine levels vary depending on factors such as bean type, roasting , and brewing methods , a Black Eye is likely to contain over 500 mg of caffeine per serving, significantly exceeding the daily recommended dose of 400 mg . Compared to a Red Eye or Depth Charge, which includes a single shot of espresso and ranges from 250-400 mg of caffeine, the Black Eye offers a more potent caffeine boost . Known for its robust and intense flavor, this drink strikes a balance between the strength of espresso and the milder taste of drip coffee .

Bodum, Inc. , (also known as BODUM) is a tableware and kitchenware company founded in Copenhagen, Denmark, in 1944 by Peter Bodum. In 1978, the son of the founder and new chief executive officer, Jørgen Bodum, moved the company to Switzerland to relocate Bodum to central Europe. Among the products Bodum makes are the Bodum French press , vacuum coffee brewers (the “Santos”), and double-walled beverage glasses made of borosilicate glass .

A boiler is a closed vessel in which water or other fluid is heated. The heated or vaporized fluid exits the boiler for use in various processes or heating applications, including boiler-based power generation, cooking, and sanitation.

Bonavita is a coffee equipment brand established in 2009, known for affordable, precision-designed brewers and kettles catering to home and professional users. It gained prominence with SCA-certified automatic drip brewers, meeting strict specialty coffee standards for temperature and extraction . The brand’s gooseneck kettles and pour-over brewers balance functionality, durability, and value, democratizing specialty coffee.

Borosilicate glass is a type of glass with the main glass-forming constituents silica and boron oxide. Borosilicate glasses are known for having very low coefficients of thermal expansion (~3 × 10 /°C at 20°C), making them resistant to thermal shock, more so than any other common glass. Such glass is less subject to thermal stress and is commonly used for the construction of reagent bottles. Borosilicate glass is sold under such trade names as Kimax, Pyrex, Endural, Schott, or Refmex.

“Brain damage” or “ Brain Injury ” (BI) refers to damage to or the loss of brain cells. These injuries can stem from a wide range of internal and external sources. In a coffee context, the term is used metaphorically to describe the catastrophic and irreversible overheating of coffee beans during roasting.

Bready coffee refers to under-roasted or underdeveloped coffee beans , characterized by flavors that suggest raw dough, bread, grains, or crackers. This descriptor means a roast defect rather than an origin-specific characteristic; any coffee bean type can develop these qualities when subjected to improper roasting techniques. The term emerged from modern specialty coffee roasting and quality control practices to diagnose and communicate roast profile flaws.

The breve is a type of espresso-based beverage comparable to a caffè latte . The term refers to an American version that uses half-and-half instead of milk. This method produces a coffee drink known for its richer, creamier character than a traditional latte.

Breville refers to an Australian appliance manufacturer founded in 1932 by Bill O’Brien and Harry Norville in Sydney. The company name combines the founders’ surnames – “Bill” and “Norville” creating “Breville” . Initially focused on radio components and mine detectors during World War II, Breville shifted to kitchen appliances in the post-war era. The brand gained prominence in the 1970s with the introduction of the sandwich toaster, which became synonymous with the Breville name in Australia and New Zealand.

Brightness in coffee refers to a pleasant, tangy acidity that creates a lively and vibrant flavor experience. This characteristic manifests as citrusy, fruity , or wine-like notes that add complexity and energy to each sip.

The Brikka Pot, Bialetti’s stovetop espresso maker , distinguishes itself from traditional moka pots through its patented weighted valve, which produces a crema-like foam layer. By dynamically regulating pressure (explained in Mechanism and Weighted Valve), the valve helps a richer, espresso-like extraction, improving texture and aroma. This results in a velvety mouthfeel and intensified flavor, merging stovetop simplicity with espresso-machine quality.

Briny describes a coffee taste that evokes the salty, savory character of seawater or brine, creating a brackish sensation on the palate. This flavor descriptor is one of the most unwelcome characteristics a coffee can have, as it alters the expected taste profile in an unpleasant direction.
Bucharest is a major coffee center, with one specialty café per 52,000 inhabitants, more than Berlin , or Copenhagen . The last years, the specialty coffee scene has grown exponentially.

Bunn-O-Matic Corporation is a manufacturer of coffee and tea-making equipment headquartered in Springfield, Illinois with a sister plant in Creston, Iowa. Founded by George Bunn, who invented the fluted coffee filter , its customers are primarily institutional foodservice providers. The company also offers a product line for home use and introduced the first commercial quality drip brewer for the home market in 1972. Its products are sold under the Bunn and Bunn-o-Matic brands.
A burr grinder uses two abrasive surfaces (burrs) to crush coffee beans to a consistent particle size, producing more uniform grounds than blade grinders for better extraction.

Cafestol is a diterpene molecule present in coffee. A typical bean of Coffea arabica contains about 0.6% cafestol by weight. Cafestol is present in its highest quantity in unfiltered coffee drinks such as French press coffee or Turkish coffee /Greek coffee. In filtered coffee drinks such as drip brewed coffee, it is present in only negligible amounts. Studies have shown that regular consumption of boiled coffee increases serum cholesterol by 8% in men and 10% in women. This increase in cholesterol, more specifically Low Density Lypoprotein (LDL) cholesterol has been linked to various cardiovascular diseases. Heavy consumption of cafestol is particularly a problem for those who have a genetic mutation that slows down metabolism of coffee in the body and is likely not an issue for the general population.

Caffè Americano, or Americano (English: American coffee) is a style of coffee prepared by adding hot water to espresso , giving it a similar strength to, but different flavor from regular drip coffee. The strength of an Americano varies with the number of shots of espresso and the amount of water added. The name is also spelled with varying capitalization and use of diacritics.

Caffeine is a bitter , white crystalline xanthine alkaloid that acts as a stimulant drug. Caffeine is found in varying quantities in the seeds, leaves, and fruit of some plants, where it acts as a natural pesticide that paralyzes and kills certain insects feeding on the plants, as well as enhancing the reward memory of pollinators.

Caffeine Extraction in Coffee Brewing Caffeine extraction occurs during the brewing process as water dissolves and pulls caffeine molecules from ground coffee. The extraction rate depends on several factors, including grind size , water temperature , and brewing time. Research shows that a standard brewing ratio of 15:1 (150g water to 10g coffee) provides optimal extraction conditions . Grind size significantly impacts extraction – finer grinds increase surface area and caffeine extraction rates.
Caffè Latte is a drink commonly prepared with one third espresso and two thirds steamed milk . The name is a portmanteau of the Italian words Caffè, which means coffee, and Latte, which means milk.

Caffè Mocha is a popular coffee beverage blending espresso, steamed milk , and chocolate, often finished with whipped cream. Its name originates from Mocha, Yemen, a historic port city renowned for its coffee trade and beans with a naturally chocolatey profile, which directly influenced the drink’s flavor concept. It serves as a chocolate-infused version of a caffè latte or a hot chocolate enhanced with espresso.

Caffè crema sometimes misspelled cafe crema, refers to two different espresso drinks. Caffè crema is an old name for espresso , and it was used in the 1940s and the 50s. The other drink named caffè crema is a long espresso drink originating in Europe. Caffè crema is primarily served in Switzerland, Austria and northern Italy, along the Italian/ Swiss and Italian/ Austrian border. Caffè crema generally means “espresso”. However, in technical discussions, referring to the long drink, it may be referred to as Swiss caffè crema.

Café Bombón (pronounced kah-FEY bohm-BON) is a traditional Spanish coffee drink and a popular variation of espresso . The drink consists of equal parts freshly brewed espresso and sweetened condensed milk. It is known for its distinct two-layer appearance, which is presented in a small clear glass. Originating from Spain ’s Valencia region, Café Bombón features a simple, sweet, and robust flavor profile.

Café Romano is a traditional Italian coffee preparation that combines espresso with lemon. It consists of a single or double shot of espresso served with either a slice of fresh lemon or lemon zest on the side.

Café au lait (French for “coffee with milk”) is a traditional coffee beverage consisting of equal parts brewed coffee and steamed milk . Unlike a latte , which uses espresso and steamed milk with microfoam , café au lait typically has regular hot milk without the frothy texture. The drink is traditionally served in a wide-brimmed bowl or large cup, making it ideal for dipping pastries .

Café con Leche ( Spanish for “coffee with milk”) is a classic beverage of equal parts strong coffee, typically espresso , and scalded or steamed milk . A staple in Spain and Latin America, it is traditionally served in a glass and is the regional equivalent of the French café au lait or Italian caffè latte .

Camp Coffee is a concentrated liquid coffee essence that was a household staple in British kitchens throughout much of the 20th century. This dark, syrupy product combines coffee extract with chicory and sugar, creating a ready-to-use concentrate that requires only the addition of hot water or milk to make an instant coffee drink. The distinctive bottle design, featuring a Scottish Highland regiment soldier being served coffee by a Sikh soldier, became an iconic image on British grocery shelves.

Cancer (medical): A broad group of diseases characterized by unregulated cell growth and the formation of malignant neoplasms (tumors) that can invade nearby tissues and spread (metastasize) through the lymphatic system and bloodstream.

A cappuccino, is an Italian coffee drink traditionally prepared with espresso, hot milk, and steamed-milk foam. Istituto Nazionale Espresso Italiano defines cappuccino as a beverage prepared with 25 ml espresso, and 100 ml steam-foamed milk. In coffee shops in North America, cappuccino is prepared with a doppio espresso and frothed milk up to 6 fl oz.

A cappuccino machine is an espresso machine equipped with a steam wand or built-in milk frother, designed to prepare espresso and steam milk for cappuccinos. These machines vary from manual models requiring skill to fully automatic ones that simplify milk frothing and espresso extraction . The steam wand, a critical component, uses pressurized steam to create microfoam, essential for the cappuccino’s creamy texture.
Capresso markets high-end coffeemakers, espresso machines, grinders, electric water kettles and frothers. The company is owned by Jura AG of Switzerland and was founded in 1994.

Caramelization refers to a form of non-enzymatic browning and a type of pyrolysis involving the thermal degradation of sugars, distinct from the Maillard reaction which requires amino acids. In coffee roasting , sucrose—the primary sugar in green coffee—breaks down through pyrolysis into simpler sugars and compounds. This process is known for generating sweet, nutty, buttery, and toffee-like flavors, while visually progressing the bean’s color from yellow through deepening browns.

Caramelly notes occupy the sweet segment of the coffee flavor wheel, positioned between chocolatey and vanilla subcategories. This descriptor refers to flavors reminiscent of caramelized sugar, butterscotch, and brown sugar in coffee. The perception of caramel sweetness is somewhat paradoxical, as research shows that roasting degrades 99 percent of sugars present in green coffee . Despite this reduction, light-roasted coffees retain approximately 2.9 percent of the original sucrose content, while medium roasts preserve only 0.9 percent .

Carbony is a flavor descriptor for coffee that evokes the aroma and taste of charcoal, burnt wood, or dark toast, typically associated with dark roasts . This profile emerges as a foundational, bitter base note that defines many traditional espresso blends, French roasts, and Italian roasts . The sensory experience centers on deep, smoky characteristics reminiscent of campfire embers or toasted bread crusts.

A Caro beverage is a caffeine-free coffee substitute made from roasted barley, malted barley, chicory, and rye, replicating coffee’s richness without the stimulant. Originating in Germany, it is commonly prepared as an instant granular drink, offering a malty , slightly bitter flavor akin to coffee. Ideal for those reducing caffeine , Caro preserves the ritual of a warm, robust beverage.

Ceramic is an excellent material for the coffee industry. Its ability to conduct heat, which can be low or high depending on its specific makeup, makes it fit for a wide array of uses. The most common applications are coffee cups and mugs, where the right thermal traits keep a drink hot without making the outside too warm to hold. Ceramic kettles and pots are also popular, prized both for holding heat well and for their visual charm. Another important use is the coffee dripper, where ceramic aids in keeping a stable brewing temperature . Furthermore, ceramic coffee grinders mark a newer development; they are highly valued because the ceramic grinding burrs do not heat the coffee beans during the process, which protects the beans’ delicate flavors and aromas. This adaptability, coming from adjustable material properties, lets ceramics meet various functional and design needs throughout the entire coffee preparation and serving journey.

A cezve is a pot designed specifically to make Turkish coffee . The body and handle are traditionally made of brass or copper (occasionally silver or gold); though, recently, cezve are more commonly made from stainless steel , aluminium, or ceramics. The long handle is particularly useful to avoid burning one’s hands, and the brim is designed to serve the coffee. Other regional variations of the word cezve are jezve and čezve. In Ukrainian and Russian, the word is spelled джезва .

Chameleon Cold Brew is a brand of organic, ready-to-drink cold brew coffee concentrate known for its smooth, low-acid profile and versatility. Founded in Austin, Texas in 2010, it helped popularize high-quality cold brew by offering a convenient, shelf-stable concentrate that could be mixed with water or milk. The brand uses beans from organic, fair-trade farms, focusing on ethical production and sustainability. Its products include black coffee concentrate and flavored varieties, catering to different consumer tastes.

Channeling (spelled Channelling in British English) refers to a critical defect in espresso brewing. This problem occurs when water under high pressure finds or creates uneven paths through the compressed coffee puck, bypassing much of the grounds.
The Chemex Coffeemaker is a manual coffeemaker. It was introduced, and continues to be manufactured, by the Chemex Corporation in Pittsfield, Massachusetts. Peter Schlumbohm invented it in 1941.

Common chicory, Cichorium intybus, is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant usually with bright blue flowers, rarely white or pink. Various varieties are cultivated for salad leaves, chicons, or for roots (var. sativum), which are baked, ground, and used for preparing a beverage. It is also grown as a forage crop for livestock. It lives as a wild plant on roadsides in its native Europe, and in North America and Australia, where it has become naturalized.

Chocolate Coffee Notes refers to a natural flavor and aroma profile in coffee that is characteristic of chocolate. This characteristic can range from sweet milk chocolate to dark chocolate or cocoa, and it develops through roasting chemistry without any added flavorings . The profile is known for adding a comforting and rich dimension to coffee, and it is a feature of many popular coffee styles.

Cholesterol, a name that comes from the Greek words for bile (*chole-*) and solid (*stereos*), plus the chemical suffix *-ol*, is an organic molecule known as a sterol. It is a basic building block of animal cell membranes, where it has the key job of maintaining proper membrane permeability and structural fluidity. Beyond this cellular role, cholesterol serves as the necessary starting point for the body to make vital substances. These include steroid hormones, bile acids for digestion, and vitamin D.

Citrus in coffee refers to flavor notes that evoke fruits such as lemon, orange, grapefruit, or lime, characterized by bright acidity and a refreshing tang . These flavors come from specific aromatic compounds present in coffee beans , which become detectable during tasting . Citrus notes appear mostly in light to medium roast coffees, with African origins—particularly Ethiopia, Kenya, and Tanzania—often showing these characteristics .

Clean coffee represents a category of high-quality, specialty coffee that prioritizes flavor clarity and artisanal production methods over mass-market approaches. This term refers to coffee produced through small-batch roasting, typically ranging from 5-25 kg per batch, which allows for precise control over the roasting process and enhanced flavor complexity.

A cocktail shaker in coffee context refers to the barware used to prepare chilled espresso -based beverages through shaking with ice. This technique produces drinks with a distinctive frothy, aerated texture that resembles cocktail preparation methods. The shaking action creates a light, foamy consistency while rapidly chilling the espresso, resulting in a refreshing beverage with an enhanced mouthfeel compared to traditional iced coffee preparations. Popular applications include the Italian Caffè Shakerato and modern specialty coffee interpretations.

Coffea is a genus of flowering plants whose seeds, called coffee beans, are used to make coffee. It is a member of the Rubiaceae family. They are shrubs or small trees native to tropical and southern Africa and tropical Asia. Coffee ranks as one of the world’s most valuable and widely traded commodity crops and is an important export product of several countries. The plant is cultivated in over 70 countries, primarily in equatorial Latin America, Southeast Asia, India, and Africa.

Arabica ( Coffea arabica) Coffea arabica, commonly known as Arabica, is the world’s most widely cultivated coffee species, accounting for approximately 60-70% of global coffee production . Native to the highlands of Ethiopia , this species grows best at elevations between 1,000-2,000 meters in subtropical climates with distinct rainy and dry seasons . Arabica beans are distinguished by their oval shape and central crease, containing less caffeine (0.8-1.4%) than Robusta varieties .

Coffea charrieriana (or Charrier coffee) is a species of flowering plant in the Rubiaceae family. It is a caffeine-free coffee found in Cameroon. This plant is the only known caffeine-free coffee plant from Central Africa. C. charrieriana was selected as one of “The Top 10 New Species” described in 2008 by The International Institute for Species Exploration at Arizona State University and an international committee of taxonomists.
Coffea liberica (or Liberian coffee) is a species of flowering plant in the Rubiaceae family. It is a coffee that is found in Liberia, West Africa.

Coffee Acidity is a fundamental sensory attribute in coffee tasting, referring to the bright, tangy, and vibrant sensation perceived on the palate, often characterized by fruity, citrus, or wine-like flavors. It is a key marker of quality and complexity, distinct from the scientific pH level of the beverage. The perceived acidity arises primarily from organic acids developed in the bean during growth, processing, and roasting.

Coffee Aroma Definition and Sensory Perception Coffee aroma refers to the complex mixture of volatile compounds that create the characteristic scent of coffee, detected primarily through the nose. The development of these aromatic compounds depends heavily on roasting temperature and duration. During roasting, green coffee seeds undergo significant chemical transformations as temperatures rise. When roasted at 180°C for varying durations, coffee develops distinct aromatic profiles based on roast level .

Coffee bloom refers to the rapid release of carbon dioxide gas that occurs when hot water first contacts freshly roasted coffee grounds. This process appears as a bubbling or swelling of the coffee grounds, often accompanied by a distinctive hissing sound. The mechanism behind blooming involves the displacement of trapped CO₂ gas that builds up during roasting . When water meets the grounds, this gas escapes rapidly, creating bubbles and temporarily preventing proper water saturation.

Coffee body, also called mouthfeel, refers to the perceived weight, thickness, and texture of coffee on the palate, ranging from thin and watery to full and syrupy. This tactile sensation occurs independently from flavor, creating the physical impression of how coffee feels in the mouth rather than how it tastes. Body is primarily influenced by the concentration of soluble solids, oils, and fine particles suspended in the brewed coffee.

Coffee Bouquet: The Aroma of Freshly Ground Coffee is the complete, complex scent released when whole coffee beans are ground . It is a key sensory characteristic in professional coffee evaluation, consisting of hundreds of volatile aromatic compounds formed during roasting . This fragrant preview is distinct from the aroma of the brewed coffee itself and plays a major role in shaping our overall perception of flavor .
Coffee brewing refers to the preparation of the coffee beverage. There are many coffee brewing methods , and the extraction method can be different for these methods.

A coffee brewing method is a distinctive coffee preparation method, with specific brewing parameters, and using specific coffee making equipment. Some of the brewing parameters that can be altered to suit a coffee brewing method are:

Water temperature during coffee brewing determines the extraction yield, the total dissolved solids , and chemical profile of the coffee. All these parameters will affect the aroma and flavor of the final cup.

The Coffee Cabinet, despite its name, has no connection to coffee roasting or brewing. Instead, it means a regional beverage popular in Rhode Island and southeastern Massachusetts—a milkshake with coffee syrup and ice cream . Rhode Islanders distinguish between “cabinets” and “milkshakes,” with the former containing ice cream and the latter being flavored milk.

Coffee concentrate is a highly concentrated coffee liquid crafted through a slow, cold extraction process—coarse coffee grounds steep in cold or room-temperature water for 12 to 24 hours before filtering. Unlike traditional hot brewing, this method yields a smooth, low-acidity concentrate valued for its versatility in both flavor and application.

A coffee puck is the dense, disc-shaped cake of spent coffee grounds left in an espresso machine’s portafilter after extraction. This compacted mass—formed by tamping fresh grounds before brewing—serves as the foundation for balanced extraction, with its structure directly affecting water flow and extraction quality.

The Coffee Quality Institute (CQI) is a nonprofit organization founded in 1996, dedicated to enhancing coffee quality and improving the livelihoods of coffee farmers globally. It is renowned for its Q Grader certification program, which standardizes cupping protocols to assess coffee quality consistently, fostering a universal language for evaluation.

A coffee sock is a reusable cloth filter, typically made of cotton or linen, used to brew coffee by holding grounds as hot water passes through. Resembling a fabric pouch, often sock-shaped, it is suspended over a cup or pot via a wire frame or handle, a hallmark of Costa Rican chorreador or Southeast Asian kopi traditions.
Explore the rich cultural traditions surrounding coffee. From cafe culture to coffee ceremonies, discover the social and cultural aspects of coffee around the world.

Extraction in the context of coffee brewing, is the process of dissolving soluble solids and emulsifying aromatic oils in water. Coffee extraction is a precise process, and there are a few parameters that will determine the taste, aroma, and strength of the brewed coffee. Correctly brewing coffee requires using the correct amount of coffee grounds, extracted to the correct degree, (largely determined by the correct time), at the correct temperature .

A coffee filter is a porous barrier, typically made of paper, cloth, or metal, used to separate coffee grounds from the brewed liquid during preparation. Its primary function is to clarify the final beverage by retaining solid particles.

Coffee grinding is a critical step in the brewing process, enabling the extraction of soluble solids, caffeine, and oils from the coffee bean. Without this process, extraction would be impossible even at high temperatures, as the compounds remain locked inside the whole bean.
Aromatic oils are used in perfumery, cosmetics, flavoring of food, and in aromatherapy.

A coffee percolator is a type of pot used to brew coffee. The name stems from the word “percolate” which means to cause (a solvent) to pass through a permeable substance especially for extracting a soluble constituent. In the case of coffee-brewing the solvent is water, the permeable substance is the coffee grounds, and the soluble constituents are the chemical compounds that give coffee its color, taste, aroma, and stimulating properties.

Coffee production is the industrial process of converting the raw fruit of the coffee plant, known as a cherry, into the finished green coffee ready for roasting . This journey from farm to roaster is crucial, as each step directly shapes the flavor profile in your cup. The process begins with harvesting, followed by the critical stage of processing—removing the fruit pulp and mucilage from the seed. The method used here, whether washed, natural, or honey processed, has a profound impact on the resulting coffee’s acidity , body , and sweetness.
Coffee tamping is the action of compacting ground coffee in an espresso portafilter with a tamp, prior to brewing .
The coffee-to-water ratio—a fundamental metric in brewing—refers to the precise relationship between the mass of ground coffee and water, expressed as a weight-based proportion (e.g., 1:15).

Coffeehouse, coffee shop, and café are related terms for an establishment which primarily serves prepared coffee or other hot beverages. It shares some of the same characteristics of a bar or restaurant, but it is different from a cafeteria. As the name suggests, coffeehouses focus on providing coffee and tea as well as light snacks.
Coffeemakers are devices or cooking appliances used to brew coffee . An appliance can also be referred to as a coffee machine.

Cold brew is a coffee preparation technique where coffee is extracted using cold water or at room temperature. Cold brew coffee is not the same as iced coffee, which refers to coffee that is brewed hot and then chilled by pouring over or adding ice.

A cold brew coffee maker is a specialized device designed for steeping coarsely ground coffee in cold or room-temperature water—typically for 12 to 24 hours—without heat. This slow extraction process yields a smooth, low-acid coffee concentrate, distinct from traditional hot-brewed methods. Most models have a built-in filter or mesh system to separate grounds from the liquid after steeping, ensuring clarity.

Complexity in Coffee: A Symphony of Flavors is a metaphorical term describing the multi-layered, evolving flavor profile in coffee tasting . Diverse sensory notes harmonize across aroma, taste, mouthfeel , and aftertaste like a musical symphony . It is a characteristic of high-quality specialty coffee , focusing on the variety and transformation of distinct flavors .

In coffee brewing, concentration is an important factor, determining the coffee strength, taste and flavor. In specialty coffee , Total Dissolved Solids concentration is an important factor. Many people are particularly interested in caffeine concentration.

Cortadito (from Spanish cortar , meaning “to cut”) refers to a Cuban espresso -based coffee drink . It is a sweetened cortado, where a shot of strong espresso is first mixed with sugar to create a creamy foam known as espumita . This mixture is then “cut” with a small amount of warm steamed or condensed milk.

A Cortado is a Spanish-origin coffee beverage consisting of one part espresso cut with an equal part of warm, lightly textured milk. The name derives from the Spanish verb ‘cortar’ (to cut), referring to how the milk cuts the espresso’s acidity. Originating in Spain’s Basque Country, it is a staple in Spanish and Portuguese cafés, defined by its small volume (4-6 oz) and balanced 1:1 to 1:2 espresso-to-milk ratio.

Cowboy Coffee refers to a traditional coffee brewing method from the American West . This method involves adding coarsely ground coffee directly to a pot of boiling water over an open fire, which produces an unfiltered immersion brew. Cowboy coffee is known for its strong flavor and practicality. It plays a role in outdoor culture, as the process uses no specialized equipment beyond a pot and a heat source.

Quality crema displays distinct visual and textural characteristics that distinguish exceptional espresso from mediocre shots. Premium crema is known for a rich golden-brown to reddish-brown color, forming a smooth, velvety layer that measures 3-5mm in thickness. This foam should persist for 2-3 minutes without dissipating quickly, maintaining complete surface coverage across the espresso shot. The texture plays a role in showing crucial quality indicators.

The crust in coffee cupping refers to the layer of coffee grounds that forms on the surface when hot water is poured over freshly ground coffee. This physical barrier develops as the grounds float and create a cohesive layer across the water’s surface.

Cuban espresso, known locally as ‘café cubano’ or ‘cafecito’, is a strong, sweetened shot of espresso that serves as a cornerstone of Cuban coffee culture . It originated in Cuba during the early 20th century, evolving from Italian espresso traditions adapted to local tastes and the availability of cheaper, darker roasted beans.
Cuisinart is a brand for small kitchen appliances , especially the food processor of the same name, one of the first to become popular in the United States .

A coffee cup is a container thatcoffeeandespresso-based drinks are served in. Coffee cupsare made of porcelain, ceramic, or tempered glass and they can have a handlefor portability. Ceramic and porcelain provide insulation , maintaining the beverage hot. Tempered glassware needs a double wall construction in order to provide insulation.

A dallah is a traditional metal coffee pot , instantly recognizable by its distinctive long, curved spout. It is specifically designed for preparing Arabic coffee , holding a place of particular importance in Saudi coffee culture . The pot is not merely a tool for brewing but a central object in the social and ceremonial serving of coffee, reflecting deep-rooted customs of hospitality and community.
Dark roast coffee is roasted beyond the second crack, producing bold, smoky, and bittersweet flavors with low acidity, full body, and oily bean surfaces.

Decaffeination refers to extracting at least 97% of caffeine from green coffee beans before roasting . The process began commercially in 1905 when Ludwig Roselius developed a benzene-based method . Today, four main techniques are used: Direct Solvent, Indirect Solvent, Swiss Water, and Carbon Dioxide.

A decanter is a vessel that is used to hold the decantation of a liquid which may contain sediment. Decanters are normally used as serving vessels for wine. Decanters vary in shape and design. They are usually made of an inert material and will hold at least one standard bottle of wine (0.75 litre). A similar kind of vessel, the carafe /kəˈræf/, is used for serving wine as well as other drinks, but is not supplied with a stopper.
Degassing is the process by which freshly roasted coffee releases CO2 gas over time, which must partially complete before brewing for optimal extraction.

Dementia (from Latin dementia , ‘madness’) refers to a medical condition characterized by a serious, progressive decline in global cognitive ability, including thinking, reasoning, memory, and emotional regulation, often resulting from widespread brain injury or neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer’s. This static, global impairment manifests as a loss of vibrancy and richness in mental function, akin to the flat, lifeless sensory experience of underdeveloped coffee beans known for a baked flavor profile.

A demitasse is a small cup used to serve Turkish coffee or espresso . In some languages it is called fincan, fildžan, filxhan or φλιτζάνι (flidzáni). In Spanish, it is called a pocillo. It typically has about 60–90 ml capacity — half the size of a full coffee cup (a tasse à café is about 120 ml). Typically they are made of white pottery or porcelain and accompanied by matching saucers, but some coffeehouses and companies from chinaalso produce brightly decorated varieties.

Descaling removes mineral buildup—primarily calcium and limescale—from coffee equipment after repeated heated water exposure. These deposits accumulate in critical components like boilers, pipes, and group heads, impairing heat transfer and restricting water flow while introducing off-flavors by disrupting extraction.

De’Longhi Group, or De’Longhi S.p. A, is a major Italian small appliance manufacturer based in Treviso, Italy. They manufacture coffee making equipment, including drip coffee makers and espresso machines.

Diabetes mellitus, commonly called diabetes, is a long-term metabolic disorder marked by consistently high blood sugar levels. The condition stems from an issue with insulin, the hormone that manages blood glucose. This problem happens either because the pancreas does not produce sufficient insulin or because the body’s cells stop responding to it properly, a state known as insulin resistance. As a result, glucose builds up in the bloodstream. This leads to the three classic signs: polyuria (frequent urination), polydipsia (increased thirst), and polyphagia (heightened hunger). Without careful management, prolonged high blood sugar can cause severe damage to the heart, blood vessels, eyes, kidneys, and nerves. The disease is primarily divided into three types: Type 1 diabetes, where the immune system attacks insulin-producing cells; Type 2 diabetes, defined by insulin resistance and often a gradual loss of insulin production; and gestational diabetes, which emerges during pregnancy. While their origins differ, all forms share the core difficulty of controlling blood sugar through a combination of medication, dietary choices, and lifestyle changes.

Dialing In (spelled dialling in in UK/ Australia ) refers to the process of adjusting an espresso machine and grinder to produce a balanced shot from a specific coffee. This daily routine involves fine-tuning several variables based on taste . The term comes from the act of turning a grinder’s dial to change the fineness of the coffee grounds, a setting that plays a crucial role in extraction.

Dissolution is the process by which a solute forms a solution in a solvent. The solute, in the case of solids, has its crystalline structure disintegrated as separate ions, atoms, and molecules form. For liquids and gases, the molecules must be adaptable with those of the solvent for a solution to form. The outcome of the process of dissolution (the amount dissolved at equilibrium.
The Nescafé Dolce Gusto is an espresso machine /coffee capsule system from Nestlé. The machines are produced by hardware manufacturers Krups and De’Longhi .
Dorian Bodnariuc is the founder of Coffee-Brewing-Methods.com . He started his coffee career as a barista, then moved in the IT, but he kept the contact with the coffee industry.

Double, in the context of espresso brewing , refers to the volume of coffee pulled at one time. A double shot of espresso is pulled from approximately 14 grams of coffee grounds. The filter basket used for pulling it, is also called a double, and it can hold 14 grams of coffee grounds. The double espresso shot is also called a doppio, the Italian word for double.

A drink, or beverage, is a kind of liquid which is specifically prepared for human consumption. There are many groups of drinks. It can be divided into various groups such as plain water, alcohol, non alcoholic drinks, soft drinks (carbonated drinks), fruit or vegetable juices and hot drinks. In addition to fulfilling a basic need, drinks form part of the culture of human society.
Drip coffee is brewed by passing hot water through a paper or metal filter containing ground coffee, with the brewed liquid dripping into a carafe below.

A drip tray is a removable grate and reservoir positioned beneath an espresso machine’s group head, serving as the first line of defense against spills by collecting excess water, stray coffee grounds, and beverage overflow during brewing. This component does more than contain mess—it prevents liquid and residue buildup that could compromise machine surfaces or countertop hygiene.

A dual boiler espresso machine features two dedicated boilers—one for brewing and another for steaming—enabling independent temperature control for simultaneous operation. Unlike single-boiler models, this design eliminates task-switching delays, ensuring precise extraction temperatures and stable steam pressure . The brew boiler optimizes flavor extraction, while the steam boiler delivers consistent microfoam for milk drinks.

Dunkin’ Donuts is an American global doughnut company and coffeehouse chain based in Canton, Massachusetts. It was founded in 1950 by William Rosenberg in Quincy, Massachusetts. Its logo is two D’s side by side in orange and hot pink. The company primarily competes with Starbucks , as over half the company’s business is in coffee sales, and with Krispy Kreme for doughnut sales.

E-61 is a class of espresso machine , defining a standard size and fitting for the portafilter which holds the ground coffee. E-61 is a common standard for commercial espresso machines. The name E-61 comes from the Faema E-61 espresso machine, which was named for the solar eclipse in its year of introduction, 1961.

An Easy Serving Espresso Pod, or E.S.E. pod, is a small coffee disc (Coffee pod), packed in a paper filter covering. Each pod contains 7 grams of compressed ground coffee, ready to be extracted into a shot. A double serving pod, (doppio), contains 14 grams of ground coffee. Pods are typically 44-45mm size for E.S.E. certified machines. There are many Espresso machines that can use the 45 mm diameter E.S.E Espresso standard Pod.

Earthy coffee presents a distinctive sensory experience characterized by rich, natural flavors that evoke soil, wood, and herbs . This flavor profile creates a connection to the earth through its deep, grounding taste sensations that coffee enthusiasts describe as reminiscent of forest floors or freshly turned garden soil. The aroma of earthy coffee typically carries notes of damp earth, mushrooms, and sometimes cedar or other woody elements .

Espressino (pronounced es-press-EE-no, from the Italian diminutive suffix ‘-ino’ meaning ‘small’) is a small Italian coffee beverage that is a regional variation of a cortado or macchiato with chocolate. It originates from the Puglia (Apulia) region in southern Italy. The drink is defined by its combination of a single shot of espresso , a small amount of frothed milk, and cocoa powder or chocolate spread.
Espresso is a concentrated coffee beverage brewed by forcing hot water under high pressure (9 bars) through finely ground, tightly packed coffee, producing a small, intense shot with crema.

Espresso beans are coffee beans roasted and blended specifically for espresso preparation, typically with a darker roast profile. While any bean can be used for espresso, those labeled as ‘espresso beans’ are optimized for high-pressure extraction , yielding a balanced, concentrated shot with lower acidity and richer body. These qualities make them ideal for milk-based drinks like lattes and cappuccinos.

An espresso blend combines beans from multiple origins, roasted and blended to create a balanced, flavorful shot when extracted under high pressure. Crafted to highlight complementary flavors, these blends emphasize sweetness, body , and acidity while ensuring batch-to-batch consistency. A well-designed blend has equal appeal in straight espresso and milk-based drinks, delivering harmony whether enjoyed alone or with dairy.
The espresso macchiato is a coffee espresso drink with a small amount of steamed milk , usually as foam, on top.
An espresso machine is a device that forces hot water under high pressure (9 bars) through finely ground coffee to produce concentrated espresso shots.

Espresso con panna, Italian for “espresso with cream,” refers to a standard shot of espresso topped with a dollop of whipped cream . The whipped cream gradually melts into the espresso, creating a sweetened and textured drinking experience without additional sugar. This preparation highlights the intensity of espresso while softening its edge with the richness of cream. Some variations include a light dusting of cocoa powder or a drizzle of caramel as optional garnishes .

The Espro P7 features a double-walled stainless steel French press design with a patented two-stage micro-filter system, minimizing sediment while preserving coffee’s natural oils and full-bodied texture. Developed by Canadian brand Espro, it combines immersion brewing benefits with a cleaner cup, eliminating paper filters entirely. Its dual precision filters (fine and ultra-fine mesh) trap grounds without over-extraction, ensuring a balanced, grit-free brew.

Ethiopia, officially the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, is a country in the Horn of Africa. It shares borders with Eritrea to the north, Djibouti and Somalia to the east, Sudan and South Sudan to the west, and Kenya to the south. With a population of over 91 million, it is the most populous landlocked country in the world and the second-most populous nation on the African continent.

Extraction time—the period from water’s initial contact with coffee grounds to the final drip—determines flavor balance by regulating the dissolution of soluble compounds: acids, sugars, and bitter elements. Shorter extractions (e.g., espresso) highlight bright acidity but may lack sweetness, yielding a sour taste. Longer extractions (e.g., immersion brewing ) risk over-extracting tannins, introducing astringency.

Extraction yield measures the percentage of coffee solids dissolved into the brewed liquid, calculated as extracted solubles relative to the original dry coffee mass. This metric shapes flavor balance by determining how much of the coffee’s key compounds (acids, sugars, and bitter elements) transfer during brewing. In specialty coffee , the 18–22% range is widely targeted for optimal extraction, where sweetness, acidity , and bitterness harmonize.

Ferment flavor in coffee refers to the distinctive sensory characteristics in the cup that develop when coffee cherries undergo controlled microbial activity during post-harvest processing. This flavor profile, valued by baristas and roasters , typically presents as bright acidity with fruity , winey , or complex notes.

Filtration is commonly the mechanical or physical operation which is used for the separation of solids from fluids (liquids or gases) by interposing a medium through which only the fluid can pass. Oversize solids in the fluid are retained, but the separation is not complete; solids will be contaminated with some fluid and filtrate will contain fine particles (depending on the pore size and filter thickness).

A Filtron is a gravity-fed cold brew coffee maker designed for slow, controlled extraction—typically one drop per second—over 12-24 hours. Modeled after Japanese Kyoto-style brewers, its three-part system (water reservoir, filter chamber, and carafe) ensures even saturation while minimizing agitation.

The Flat White is a distinct coffee preparation that emerged from Australia and New Zealand before gaining international popularity. Traditionally served in a 180 ml ceramic cup in Australia, the Flat White contains less milk than the Australian latte, which typically comes in a 200 ml glass . This smaller milk-to-coffee ratio creates a more concentrated flavor profile. Size specifications vary globally, with the authentic Flat White measuring approximately 162 ml (5.5 oz) .

A flat white is a coffee beverage consisting of espresso topped with microfoam-textured milk . Distinguished by its velvety texture and strong coffee flavor, it is typically served in a small cup (5-8oz/150-240ml) to maintain a coffee-forward profile .

Flavor or flavour is the sensory impression of a foods, drinks, or other substances, and is determined mainly by the chemical senses of taste and smell. The “trigeminal senses”, which detect chemical irritants in the mouth and throat as well as temperature and texture, are also very important to the overall Gestalt of flavor perception. The flavor of the food, as such, can be altered with natural or artificial flavorants, which affect these senses.

Flavored coffee refers to coffee beans treated with natural or artificial flavoring agents—typically after roasting—to create distinct aromatic and taste profiles. These oil-based flavorings, ranging from vanilla to seasonal spices, originated to enhance lower-quality beans but now cater to consumers seeking consistent, dessert-like experiences without extra additives.

Floral notes in coffee represent aromatic and flavor characteristics that evoke flowers, ranging from delicate jasmine and rose to bright lavender and orange blossom. These sensory qualities emerge from complex interactions between coffee origin, post-harvest processing methods, roasting techniques, and brewing parameters. Processing methods influence floral expression.

Flow rate quantifies the speed of water moving through coffee grounds during brewing, measured in grams per second. In espresso, this metric tracks water exiting the portafilter; for pour-overs, it governs drainage through the filter. This critical variable shapes extraction, influencing contact time and extraction outcomes.
Foam is an important aspect of coffee preparation, and it determines, or validates quality in some coffee drinks.

Food is any substance consumed to provide nutritional support for the body . It is usually of plant or animal origin, and contains essential nutrients, such as carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, or minerals. The substance is ingested by an organism and assimilated by the organism’s cells in an effort to produce energy, maintain life, or stimulate growth. Historically, people secured food through two methods: hunting and gathering, and agriculture.

FrancisFrancis! is an espresso machine manufacturer owned by illy. Founded in 1994 by Francesco Illy , FrancisFrancis produces espresso machines for the home market. Italian architect Luca Trazzi was responsible for the aesthetics. In 2004 the company was purchased by illy. Since then, FrancisFrancis! have become the espresso machines of choice for illy; always associated with the coffee brand. Various FrancisFrancis! machines are designed by other award-winning designers and are considered a piece of industrial art on their own. The Francis Francis! espresso makers were some of the first to feature the option of E.S.E. pods. Later on, illy introduced the iperEspresso system which produces one of the best capsule based espresso beverages.

Frappuccino is a trademarked line of blended coffee beverages sold by Starbucks . It consists of coffee , blended with ice and other various ingredients, usually topped with whipped cream. Frappuccinos are also sold as bottled coffee beverages in stores and from vending machines.

The Frappé is a shaken or blended iced coffee beverage famously reliant on instant coffee as its base. This choice highlights the tension between accessibility and specialty values. Nearly 50 percent of the world’s coffee crop is processed into instant coffee. For coffee professionals, the Frappé is known for its unique preparation method, where agitation creates a stable, creamy foam without dairy. This technique plays a role in understanding emulsion and texture in other coffee applications, from whipped coffee to shaken espresso .

French drip is a manual coffee brewing method that uses a special carafe. The carafe has a filter and a lid that are placed on top. The brewing technique is similar to other manual drip coffee brewing methods . Coffee is coarsely ground and placed in the filter. The filter is placed on top of the carafe, and it is designed to fit snugly. Then hot water is poured over the coffee grounds. The filter retains the grounds, while brewed coffee passes through in the pot. At the end the filter is covered with a lid that prevents coffee from getting cold.
The French press is a full-immersion brewing method where coarsely ground coffee steeps in hot water before a metal mesh plunger is pressed down to separate grounds from the brew.

Fruity notes in coffee refer to the aromatic and flavor characteristics reminiscent of various fruits detected during a coffee cupping or brew evaluation . These notes are categorized into distinct sensory groups central to coffee flavor profiling. Berry notes include raspberry and blueberry characteristics prized in some African coffees, while citrus covers lemon and orange impressions. Stone fruit notes show peach and plum qualities, and tropical fruit notes include pineapple and passion fruit .

Full immersion is a coffee brewing method where ground coffee remains fully submerged in water throughout extraction, ensuring even saturation and uniform flavor development. Unlike percolation methods—which pass water through grounds once—full immersion maintains continuous contact, yielding a balanced, full-bodied cup. This approach prioritizes control, enabling precise adjustment of steep time, temperature, and agitation to influence extraction.

Gaggia is an Italian company that makes coffee machines, especially espresso and cappuccino machines, in addition to small kitchen appliances . The company is mainly owned by Saeco International Group, a division of Dutch consumer electronics giant Philips.

The Gaggia Classic Pro is an entry-level semi-automatic espresso machine crafted by Italian manufacturer Gaggia for home use. Designed with commercial-grade components like a 58mm portafilter and a three-way solenoid valve, it bridges professional and domestic espresso-making. Its robust construction and straightforward design make it ideal for mastering techniques such as shot extraction and milk texturing.

Galão ( Portuguese pronunciation: [ɡɐˈlɐ̃w̃]) refers to a traditional Portuguese hot coffee drink . It consists of one part espresso combined with three parts foamed milk, served in a tall glass. This beverage is a type of Portugal’s standard café-style latte and is known for its mild, creamy flavor profile. The name translates to “gallon,” which means the drink’s substantial milk volume.

A God shot can be described as a perfect shot achieved from an espresso machine, where the recipe and all of the parameters that go into espresso brewing such as bean type, roast, grind size , dose, water volume and temperature , as well as properly maintained and clean machinery all align to produce a coffee shot that is considered to be perfect by the taster, barista or customer.

Grassy notes in coffee represent a distinct flavor characteristic that manifests as fresh-cut grass, hay, or herbaceous qualities in the cup. These flavors typically indicate underdeveloped coffee beans or processing issues that prevent proper flavor maturation during roasting. The identification and classification of such defects is known for increasing sophistication through research initiatives.

The grouphead is the component of an espresso machine where the portafilter attaches, housing the dispersion screen and gasket that distribute hot water evenly to the coffee puck. It functions as the critical interface between the machine and the coffee, enabling precise water distribution and temperature control during extraction.

Hamilton Beach Brands, Inc. is an American manufacturer of home appliances , air purifiers, and commercial restaurant equipment marketed primarily in the United States, Canada , and Mexico including: Blenders, Mixers, Toasters, Slow cookers, Irons and Air purifiers. Until sometime in the 1980s the company’s products were marketed under the brand name “Hamilton Beach Scovill”, reflecting a merger that occurred in the 1940s.

Handpresso SARL is a French manufacturer of portable espresso machines . Founded in Fontainebleau in 2006 by Henrik Nielsen as a spin-off from Nielsen Innovation SARL. Handpresso is inspired by Danish Design and has created and patented the world’s first handheld espresso coffeemaker, Handpresso WILD ESE, which is sold in 25 countries. The first Handpresso machines were designed for E.S.E. coffee pods . In the year 2008, Handpresso won 7 international design prizes including IF and Formland.

Hario is a Japanese company specializing in high-quality glassware and coffee brewing equipment, renowned for its V60 pour-over dripper. Founded in 1921 as a manufacturer of laboratory glass, Hario transitioned to coffee products, leveraging its expertise in heat-resistant materials to create precise, durable tools. The V60, introduced in the 2000s, features a distinctive cone shape with spiral ribs, promoting even extraction.
The Hario V60 is a cone-shaped pour-over dripper with spiral ridges and a large single hole, allowing precise control over flow rate and extraction.

Harsh coffee represents an undesirable flavor profile characterized by sharp, aggressive, and unpleasant sensory experiences. This negative descriptor includes off-putting characteristics that make coffee difficult to enjoy, typically featuring bitter compounds that create an astringent, mouth-puckering sensation. These flavors often present as metallic, acrid, or burning notes that linger.

The heart is a hollow muscle that pumps blood throughout the blood vessels by repeated, rhythmic contractions . It is found in all animals with a circulatory system. The term cardiac means “related to the heart” and comes from the Greek καρδιά, kardia, for “heart”.

A heat exchanger is a piece of equipment built for efficient heat transfer from one medium to another. The media may be separated by a solid wall, so that they never mix, or they may be in direct contact. They are widely used in space heating, refrigeration, air conditioning, power plants, chemical plants, petrochemical plants, petroleum refineries, natural gas processing, and sewage treatment.

Definition and Lexicon Placement “Herbal” serves as a primary descriptor in coffee tasting vocabulary, identifying flavor notes that resemble fresh or dried herbs such as sage, thyme, basil, or oregano. This term occupies a distinct position within established coffee flavor lexicons, including the Specialty Coffee Association’s Flavor Wheel, where it falls under the broader category of plant-like qualities .

A hermetic seal has the quality of being airtight. In common usage, the term often implies being impervious to air or gas. When used technically, it is stated in conjunction with a specific test method and conditions of usage.

Hidey is a coffee tasting term describing a specific, often undesirable, flavor note in a brew, reminiscent of animal hides or leather . This descriptor emerged in professional cupping to identify a pungent savory note that differs from standard earthy defects in a roast . It captures an animalistic quality that separates it from other off-flavors in the coffee lexicon.

High-density lipoprotein (HDL) is one of the five main types of lipoproteins that carry fats like cholesterol and triglycerides through the watery environment of the blood. These particles are often listed by size, from the largest to the smallest: chylomicrons, very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL), intermediate-density lipoprotein (IDL), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) , and finally HDL. In a person with good health, roughly thirty percent of the total blood cholesterol is transported by HDL particles. Standard blood tests measure HDL-C, which refers specifically to the amount of cholesterol found inside these HDL carriers.

Home appliances are electrical/mechanical machines which accomplish some household functions, such as cooking or cleaning. Home appliances can be classified into: Major appliances, or White goods, Small appliances, or Brown goods Consumer electronics, or Shiny goods. The consumer electronics division is also notable for the maintenance and repair of these kinds of products.

Hot chocolate, traditionally made from melted chocolate or cocoa powder mixed with milk or water, is sweetened and enhanced with vanilla or spices. As a caffeine-free option, it holds a significant place in coffee culture, historically served in European coffeehouses alongside espresso drinks. Today, specialty cafés treat it with the same care as coffee, using high-quality cocoa and refined techniques.

A hot plate is a small, portable tabletop appliance that has one or more electric heating elements or gas burners. This self-contained unit works on its own but often acts as a substitute for a single burner from a full-sized stove . Its compact and standalone design makes it a highly versatile tool for locations without a full kitchen, including dormitory rooms, office break areas, small apartments, and outdoor spaces. The device offers a direct and adjustable source of heat for various cooking jobs such as boiling water, simmering sauces, or frying foods. Its simplicity and portability have secured its place in both domestic and professional settings where a permanent cooking installation is impractical or unavailable.

Hypertension (HTN or arterial hypertension) is a chronic condition of elevated arterial blood pressure , summarized by systolic pressure—the higher number measuring arterial pressure during heartbeats when the heart muscle contracts—and diastolic pressure—the lower number measuring pressure between beats when the heart is relaxed. This elevation requires the heart to work harder than normal.
An iced latte typically refers to a beverage that is prepared with freshly brewed, hot espresso and chilled milk over ice. This drink is very typical in the United States.

Iced coffee is a cold variant of coffee. In more recent times it has become common for coffee shops to offer ‘iced’ versions of their most popular coffee drinks. The iced latte and iced mocha are the two most common examples of this. A quick way of preparing such drinks is to make a small quantity of strong, hot espresso , dissolving the required sweetener/flavorings in the hot liquid and then pouring this directly into a cup of ice cold milk. This method is common in busier coffee shops. The hot coffee can also be cooled using cold water, ice, cream or ice cream.
The iced mocha is a variant of the iced latte and another beverage that would fall into the bracket of iced coffee .

illycaffè is a brand of coffee produced in Trieste, Italy. illy produces principally one blend in three roast variations: normal, dark roast , and decaffeinated. The blend is packaged as whole beans, pre-ground coffee, E.S.E. pods , or iperEspresso Capsules.
Immersion brewing is any method where coffee grounds are fully submerged in water for the entire brew time, allowing for even extraction and consistent results.

Immersion cold brew is a coffee preparation method where coarsely ground coffee steeps in cold or room-temperature water for 12 to 24 hours before filtration. Unlike drip or flash-chilled methods, immersion brewing achieves full saturation of grounds, allowing a slow, balanced extraction that boosts sweetness while cutting acidity.

Indian Filter Coffee refers to a distinctive coffee beverage characterized by its thick, syrupy consistency and robust flavor profile. The drink is prepared using a traditional two-chamber metal filter device specific to South Indian coffee culture . The coffee consists of pre-ground arabica and/or robusta beans blended with chicory—sometimes in ratios as high as 50:50 . This unique composition gives the beverage its strong, distinctive taste.

Inka is a Polish roasted grain beverage and brand. Developed in the late 1960s during communist rule, Inka has been produced in Skawina since 1971, a centre of coffee production since the early 20th century. Presently it is manufactured by GRANA Sp. Z O.O. While it was used in part as a coffee substitute to alleviate coffee shortages in the 1970s, Inka remains popular, in part to the fact that it is caffeine-free.

Instant taste describes the distinctive sensory profile of instant coffee, characterized by a concentrated flavor that differs from traditionally brewed coffee. The taste results from the extraction process where coffee grounds undergo pressurized water treatment at 175°C (347°F), producing a concentrated brew containing 25% to 60% extracted soluble compounds. This concentrated extraction creates a flavor profile that tends toward intensity rather than complexity . The sweetness component plays a crucial role in instant coffee’s taste profile.

Ipoh White Coffee is a distinctive Malaysian coffee beverage that originated in the city of Ipoh, located in the state of Perak . This specialty drink differs from conventional coffee through its unique roasting process , where green coffee beans are roasted at lower temperatures between 325°F and 375°F, creating a lighter-colored bean with reduced bitterness .

Irish coffee is a hot coffee cocktail that combines a strong coffee brew, Irish whiskey, sugar, and a layer of cream on top . This beverage is traditionally served in a clear glass mug, which shows its distinct layered appearance valued in coffee presentation . The standard preparation includes approximately 30ml (1oz) of Irish whiskey, though premium versions might use specific varieties such as Jameson 12-year or Redbreast .

James Hoffmann is a British coffee expert, author, and 2007 World Barista Champion whose work has redefined specialty coffee culture. As co-founder of London’s Square Mile Coffee Roasters, he gained global recognition through his YouTube channel and *The World Atlas of Coffee*. This guide translates coffee’s complexities for professionals and enthusiasts alike, blending scientific precision with approachable storytelling.
Joshua Spink is an Irish opera singer and writer. His specialist topics are coffee, food, wellness and culture.
