Jura Elektroapparate AG is a Swiss developer and distributor of home appliances , headquartered in Niederbuchsiten, Canton of Solothurn. The company was founded in 1931 by Leo Henzirohs. Formerly, Jura ran its own factory, but outsourced production to outside companies in the 1990s. Jura is currently best known for its fully automatic espresso machines . This core area originated in the early 1980s and is nowadays a main element of the brand image as well as creating most of its sales. The espresso machines are produced by Eugster/Frismag in Romanshorn, which also makes coffee machines for Siemens, Bosch and AEG.

Kahweol is a diterpene molecule found in the beans of Coffea arabica . It is structurally related to cafestol . Recent research suggests that kahweol may have beneficial effects on bone by inhibiting osteoclast differentiation. Another recent study confirmed that kahweol has anti-inflammatory and anti-angiogenic effects, offering a possible mechanism for the association found in epidemiological studies between consumption of unfiltered coffee and decreased risk of cancer .

Kalita is a Japanese coffee equipment manufacturer known for its distinctive pour-over brewing devices, particularly the Kalita Wave dripper. This flat-bottomed dripper features three small holes that regulate water flow and promote even extraction , contributing to a consistent and balanced brew.

Karsk (from Old Norse karskr , meaning vigorous), also known as kask or kaffekask , refers to a traditional Scandinavian cocktail. It consists of strong, hot black coffee and high-proof neutral spirits, typically moonshine or vodka. This warming drink originates from rural Scandinavia and is a type of utilitarian beverage distinct from cream-topped cocktails like Irish coffee . Karsk is known for its unique preparation method, which involves using a coin to measure the balance between coffee and alcohol.

A kettle, sometimes called a tea kettle or teakettle, is a type of pot, typically metal, specialized for boiling water over a heat source, with a lid, spout and handle, or a small kitchen appliance of similar shape that functions in a self-contained manner. Kettles can be heated either by placing on a stove, or by their own internal electric heating element in the appliance versions.

Keurig, is a North American manufacturer of coffee brewers for both home and commercial use. It is a part of Green Mountain Coffee Roasters , Inc. (GMCR). Keurig is based in Massachusetts. Their best selling products are the single serve coffee machine Keurig, and the coffee capsules for the brewer.

A kitchen is a room or part of a room used for cooking and food preparation. In the West, a modern residential kitchen is typically equipped with a stove , a sink with hot and cold running water, a refrigerator and kitchen cabinets arranged according to a modular design. Many households have a microwave oven, a dishwasher and other electric appliances.

KitchenAid is an American home appliance brand owned by Whirlpool Corporation. The company was started in 1919 by The Hobart Corporation to produce stand mixers; the “H-5” was the first model introduced. The company faced stiff competition as rivals moved into this emerging market, and introduced its trademarked silhouette in the 1930s with the model “K”, the work of designer Egmont Arens.

Kopi Tubruk (from the Javanese word for ‘collision’) is a traditional Indonesian coffee brewing method where coarsely or medium-ground coffee is steeped directly in hot water without filtration . It is an unfiltered immersion brew, similar in concept to a rustic cowboy coffee . The grounds settle at the bottom of the cup, creating a strong, full-bodied beverage often called ‘mud coffee.’

Krups is a German kitchen appliance manufacturer, named after its founder Robert Krups. It is often confused with the Krupp conglomerate. The company also produces a large variety of household appliances. Krups competes with De’Longhi, Sunbeam, Braun, Russell Hobbs, Bosch and Black & Decker .

A latte, which translates from Italian as “coffee milk,” is a popular coffee drink built on a foundation of espresso and steamed milk . In English, the word is occasionally misspelled as latté or lattè, with the added accent mark considered a hyperforeignism—an attempt to make the word seem more authentically foreign than it is. Interestingly, the term ‘ Café au lait ’ has historically been used for espresso with milk in Northern Europe and Scandinavia. In the United States, however, that same phrase typically refers to a combination of brewed coffee and steamed milk, highlighting a key regional difference in coffee terminology.
Latte art is the technique of pouring steamed milk into espresso to create patterns or designs on the surface of the drink, demonstrating barista skill and milk quality.

Latte Macchiato refers to a hot milk beverage ‘stained’ with espresso, distinguished by its three-layer presentation . Originating in Italy during the 1980s, it emerged as a response to American-style caffè lattes, designed to emphasize the espresso ‘mark’ more prominently .

Luigi Lavazza S.p.A. is an Italian manufacturer of coffee products. Founded in Turin in 1895 by Luigi Lavazza, it was initially run from a small grocery store at Via San Tommaso 10. The business of Lavazza S.p.A. is currently administered by the third and fourth generation of the Lavazza family.

Lelit, an Italian espresso machine manufacturer founded in 1993 in Casella d’Asolo, specializes in compact yet high-performance home equipment. By incorporating commercial-grade components—PID temperature controllers, stainless steel boilers, and E61 group heads—Lelit achieves professional-level precision in temperature stability and extraction consistency.
Light roast coffee is roasted to an internal temperature of 180-205 degrees C, preserving the bean origin flavors with high acidity, light body, and no surface oils.
A long black is a style of coffee, most commonly found in Australia , New Zealand and Brazil. It is now becoming available in the UK, predominantly in London.

Low-density lipoprotein (LDL) is one of the five major groups of lipoproteins, which in order of size, largest to smallest, are chylomicrons, VLDL, IDL, LDL, and HDL, that enable transport of multiple different fat molecules, including cholesterol , within the water around cells and within the water-based bloodstream. Studies have shown that higher levels of type-B LDL particles (as opposed to type-A LDL particles) are associated with health problems, including cardiovascular disease.
A lungo is a long espresso shot brewed with double the water of a standard espresso, producing a larger, milder, and slightly more bitter cup.

A macchiato is an espresso-based drink made with a single or double shot of espresso, lightly ‘marked’ with steamed milk or foam. Derived from the Italian *caffè macchiato* (‘stained coffee’), its name refers to the espresso’s delicate milk accent. This method softens the espresso’s intensity—mellowing acidity and bitterness—while keeping its bold core, creating a balanced yet potent profile.

Malty describes a coffee flavor characteristic that evokes the taste and aroma of malted grains, particularly those used in brewing beer or making malted milk products. This tasting note presents as a sweet, grain-forward flavor with subtle nutty undertones and a smooth, rounded mouthfeel. It shows a cereal-like sweetness reminiscent of barley malt, wheat, or oats, creating a comforting and familiar taste profile. Coffee with malty characteristics often has a medium body with low to moderate acidity.

A manual espresso machine is a lever-operated device that uses human force to generate the pressure required for espresso extraction, bypassing the need for an electric pump. Originating with the 1948 Gaggia lever machine, it revolutionized espresso-making by introducing high-pressure extraction, which produces the signature crema.

Mark Prince is a leading voice in the online coffee and espresso community. He is the founder and webmaster of the influential websites CoffeeGeek and CoffeeKid . His acknowledged expertise and passion for coffee have made him a sought-after source for interviews with various newspapers, magazines, and radio programs.

A Marocchino refers to a classic Italian coffee drink known for its distinct layered presentation. It consists of a shot of espresso , a layer of cocoa powder, and a topping of milk froth . The drink is served in a small, clear glass to show its structure and has a balanced combination of bitter, sweet, and creamy flavors.

A Mason jar—a glass jar with a screw-on lid—was originally designed for home canning but has become indispensable in coffee preparation, particularly for cold brew. Its simplicity and affordability shine in this method, where coarsely ground coffee steeps in cold water before filtering. The wide mouth simplifies filling and cleaning, while the airtight seal maintains freshness during extended steeping.

Mazagran is a distinctive, refreshing coffee beverage with origins in Algeria. It consists of strong coffee or espresso mixed with an equal portion of cold water. The drink is often sweetened and is known as a historical precursor to modern iced coffee .

Medicinal (Coffee Term) In coffee terminology, “medicinal” refers to the health-promoting bioactive compounds naturally present in coffee beans . Research indicates that moderate coffee consumption (1-5 cups daily) gives beneficial compounds with potential therapeutic effects . These include caffeine (50-400 mg/day), which at appropriate doses helps various physiological functions without triggering adverse effects like anxiety or sleep disturbances that appear at higher intakes (>500 mg/day) .
Medium roast coffee is roasted between the first and second crack, offering a balance of origin flavors and roast characteristics with moderate acidity and body.

A medium dark roast is a coffee roast level defined by beans that reach a deep brown color with visible surface oil, producing a cup with balanced bittersweet flavors, moderate acidity , and a fuller body .

Melitta is a German-based company selling coffee, paper coffee filters , and coffee makers as part of the Melitta Group, which also has Melitta branches in other countries world-wide. The company is headquartered in Minden, North Rhine-Westphalia. It is named after Melitta Bentz (1873–1950) who founded the company after she invented the drip brew paper coffee filter (German patent granted July 8, 1908). Bentz later ran the company as a family business.

Mellow Coffee Flavor A mellow coffee presents a balanced sensory profile characterized by smoothness and subdued acidity. This flavor profile typically develops in medium roasts, where beans reach internal temperatures of 410°F to 430°F, falling between first and second crack . The resulting cup offers gentle, rounded flavor notes without sharp peaks or valleys in taste perception. Mellow coffees have a soft mouthfeel that coats the palate evenly, creating a sensation often described as silky or velvety.

Melya is a distinctive coffee drink characterized by its simple yet flavorful combination of brewed coffee , honey, and a dusting of cocoa powder . It offers a sweet, rich, and slightly bitter profile, serving as a comforting and dessert-like alternative to traditional black coffee. While its exact origins are debated, its name derives from the French and Spanish word “miel,” meaning honey, highlighting a core ingredient .

Microfoam is a smooth, dense emulsion of steamed milk and tiny air bubbles, formed through precise aeration and texturing with an espresso machine’s steam wand. Its velvety, glossy texture—reminiscent of wet paint—sets it apart from frothier or unevenly steamed milk, a distinction critical for specialty coffee .
A milk frother is a device that aerates milk to create foam or microfoam for lattes, cappuccinos, and other espresso-based milk drinks.

The name ‘Mocha’ originates from the port city of Al Mokha in Yemen, a major coffee trading hub from the 15th to 17th centuries. This port was the primary gateway for Arabian coffee to reach Europe, establishing Yemen as one of the earliest commercial coffee exporters.

Mocha Java represents the world’s oldest recorded coffee blend, combining beans from Yemen’s port of Mocha (also spelled Mokha) and the Indonesian island of Java . This classic pairing balances the wild, fruity intensity of Yemeni beans with the earthy, full-bodied character of Javanese coffee. The blend originated in the 15th-16th centuries when ships from the Dutch East India Company transported both varieties to European markets .

Invented by Alfonso Bialetti in 1933, the Moka Express revolutionized home coffee brewing with its stovetop design, producing concentrated, espresso-like coffee through steam pressure . Its three-chamber system—comprising a bottom chamber for water, a middle basket for grounds, and an upper chamber for the brew—combines simplicity with efficiency.
A moka pot is a stovetop coffee maker that uses steam pressure to force boiling water through finely ground coffee, producing a strong, espresso-like brew.

Mr. Coffee is a owned by Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a Jarden Consumer Solutions and is a registered product of Newell Brands . The Mr. Coffee brand manufactures automatic-drip kitchen coffee machines as well as other products.

A mug is a sturdily built type of cup often used for drinking hot beverages, such as coffee , tea, or hot chocolate . Mugs often have handles and hold a larger amount of fluid than other types of cup. Usually a mug holds approximately 12 fluid ounces (350 mL) of liquid; double a tea cup. A mug is a less formal style of drink container and is not usually used in formal place settings, where a teacup or coffee cup is preferred.

A coffee percolator is a type of pot used to brew coffee . The name stems from the word “percolate” which means to cause (a solvent ) to pass through a permeable substance especially for extracting a soluble constituent. In the case of coffee-brewing the solvent is water, the permeable substance is the coffee grounds , and the soluble constituents are the chemical compounds that give coffee its color, taste , aroma, and stimulating properties.

Myocardial infarction (MI) or acute myocardial infarction (AMI), commonly known as a heart attack, results from the partial interruption of blood supply to a part of the heart , causing heart cells to die. This is most commonly due to occlusion (blockage) of a coronary artery following the rupture of a vulnerable atherosclerotic plaque, which is an unstable collection of lipids ( cholesterol and fatty acids) and white blood cells in the wall of an artery.

The National Coffee Association (NCA) or (National Coffee Association of U.S.A. , Inc. ), is the main market research, consumer information, and lobbying association for the coffee industry in the United States . Surveys produced by the NCA are widely cited in mainstream media. The association has numerous functions and services that include: Market and scientific research Domestic and international government relations, including lobbying Public relations and education.

Natural rubber , also called India rubber or caoutchouc, as initially produced, consists of suitable polymers of the organic compound isoprene with minor impurities of other organic compounds plus water. Forms of polyisoprene that are useful as natural rubbers are classified as elastomers. Currently the rubber is harvested mainly in the form of the latex from certain trees. The latex is a sticky, milky colloid drawn off by making incisions into the bark and collecting the fluid in vessels.

Nescafé is a brand of instant coffee made by Nestlé. It comes in many different product forms. The name is a portmanteau of the words “ Nestlé ” and “café“. Nestlé’s flagship powdered coffee product was introduced in Switzerland on April 1, 1938 after being developed for seven or eight years by Max Morgenthaler.

Nespresso is the brand name of Nestlé Nespresso S.A. , an operating unit of the Nestlé Group based in Lausanne, Switzerland. Nespresso machines brew espresso from coffee capsules, a type of pre-apportioned single-use container of ground coffee and flavorings.

Nestlé S.A. is a Swiss multinational nutritional, snack food, and health-related consumer goods company headquartered in Vevey, Switzerland. It is the largest food company in the world measured by revenues. Nestlé’s products include baby food, bottled water, breakfast cereals, coffee, confectionery, dairy products, ice cream, pet foods and snacks.

Neutral flavor serves as the reference point against which coffee professionals evaluate all other taste characteristics. This baseline represents a clean, balanced cup with no dominant flavor notes – neither overly acidic nor bitter, without pronounced sweetness or astringency . Professional tasters use neutral coffee as their calibration standard before evaluating samples with distinct regional or processing characteristics. The neutral cup has subtle grain-like or nutty undertones without sharp edges or overwhelming intensity.

New Orleans is a major United States port and the largest city and metropolitan area in the state of Louisiana . The population of the city was 343,829 as of the 2010 U.S. Census . The New Orleans metropolitan area (New Orleans– Metairie –Kenner Metropolitan Statistical Area) had a population of 1,167,764 in 2010 and was the 46th largest in the United States. The New Orleans–Metairie–Bogalusa Combined Statistical Area, a larger trading area, had a 2010 population of 1,214,932.
Nitro cold brew is cold brew coffee infused with nitrogen gas, served on tap to create a creamy, cascading texture similar to a stout beer.

Normale, in the context of espresso, is the standard way of extracting a shot. A single shot normale is obtained by extracting approximately 1 oz of coffee, using 7 grams of ground coffee. A single is often named solo, using the Italian word for it. A normale is the standard espresso concentration , whereas ristretto is a concentrated version, and lungo is the diluted version of it.

Nose in coffee tasting refers to the systematic evaluation of coffee aroma during the cupping process, representing a critical stage in professional coffee assessment. This evaluation occurs after the initial fragrance assessment of dry grounds. The process begins when boiled water is added to the coffee grounds, which are then allowed to steep for 4 minutes.

Nutty flavor in coffee represents one of the most recognizable and beloved taste profiles, characterized by distinct notes reminiscent of almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts, or pecans. This sensory experience typically shows as a warm, rich undertone that adds depth and complexity to the cup without overwhelming other flavor components.

Oxo Good Grips, a product line by OXO, specializes in ergonomic kitchen tools featuring soft, non-slip handles and user-friendly designs. Within the coffee realm, the brand provides precision tools such as gooseneck kettles, scales, and frothing pitchers, essential for achieving consistency in brewing and milk texturing.

Oliang ( โอเลี้ยง ), also known as Thai iced coffee , is a popular and distinctive coffee beverage from Thailand. It is characterized by its unique blend of robusta coffee beans roasted together with grains like corn and soybeans, and often spices like cardamom or star anise, resulting in a deeply aromatic, nutty, smoky, and strong brew .

Oniony in Coffee Definition and Sensory Profile “Oniony” refers to an off-flavor in coffee characterized by distinct allium notes reminiscent of raw or cooked onions. This defect has a sharp, pungent aroma that can range from subtle to overwhelming, often accompanied by a savory, sulfurous taste that lingers unpleasantly on the palate. The onion character typically emerges during cupping evaluation as the coffee cools, becoming more pronounced at lower temperatures (room temperature ) than when hot (~70°C) .

Osteoporosis is a skeletal disease characterized by reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and deterioration of bone microarchitecture, including trabecular bone loss. This leads to compromised bone tensile strength, mineralization, and repair processes due to reduced collagen type I and an altered ratio of non-collagenous proteins to collagen. The consequence is an increased risk of fracture from minor impacts or falls.

An over pressure valve (OPV) is a one-way vent installed in coffee packaging to release carbon dioxide emitted by freshly roasted beans while blocking oxygen ingress. As coffee degasses post-roast, CO₂ buildup can inflate or rupture bags without a controlled escape. The OPV ensures package integrity by allowing gas to exit while maintaining a sealed environment.

Oxidation is the chemical reaction between oxygen and the volatile compounds in roasted coffee, altering its flavor and aroma over time. This process begins immediately after roasting as the beans release carbon dioxide and interact with air, breaking down the delicate oils and organic compounds responsible for coffee’s complex taste.

In the coffee maker industry, a PID controller improves brewing precision by keeping the water temperature within a tight, desired range. This is especially critical for espresso, where even a few degrees can change a shot from perfectly balanced to unpleasantly sour or bitter . By replacing older, less responsive thermostats, the PID brings a level of temperature control once found only in professional machines to a wider market, directly impacting the quality and consistency of the final cup.

A Panarello steam wand is a frothing attachment for home espresso machines, featuring a plastic sleeve that fits over a standard steam wand. Its built-in air-intake hole automatically aerates milk, simplifying microfoam creation for beginners. Unlike traditional steam wands, it mechanically introduces air, producing consistently thick foam with minimal skill.

Paper filters are thin, disposable sheets of porous paper designed to hold ground coffee while allowing water to pass through. Patented by Melitta Bentz in 1908, they are essential for pour-over drippers and automatic coffee makers. By trapping fine particles and oils, they produce a clean, sediment-free cup with bright clarity, enhancing delicate flavors in light to medium roasts.

Papery flavor represents a negative taste descriptor for coffee, characterized by a dry, thin, and flat taste reminiscent of wet paper or cardboard . This unwanted sensory profile creates an unpleasant drinking experience that masks the coffee’s intended flavor characteristics. Coffee professionals categorize papery flavor as a type of ‘ taint ‘ or ‘off-flavor’ related to staleness and oxidation , rather than a roast defect or inherent bean characteristic .
Past crop refers to coffee beans from a harvest that is more than 12 months past its harvest date, having undergone significant physical and chemical changes due to prolonged storage.

Peaberry Coffee was a coffee shop chain that was started in Denver , Colorado in 1990 by Bill Tointon. The store’s concept was founded on serving a variety of coffee from all over the world and roasting it in Denver. It was categorized in a menu format called the “Peaberry Profile System”. The system offered four selections of coffee roasting styles, Light & Mild, Rich & Creamy, Extravagant & Exotic and Dark & Intense.

Peasy refers to a specific off-flavor in coffee characterized by distinct vegetal notes reminiscent of raw green peas or bell peppers . This undesirable taste attribute typically manifests when coffee has been under-roasted or when beans have not fully developed during the roasting process before reaching pyrolysis at approximately 465°F (240°C) . In sensory evaluation, peasy notes present a sharp, somewhat astringent mouthfeel accompanied by a lingering aftertaste that lacks sweetness.

Pero is a brand of caffeine-free roasted grain beverages. It is historically sold under names such as Pero. Some consider it a coffee substitute . It is manufactured by Nestlé and was first introduced in West Germany in 1954.

Koninklijke Philips Electronics N.V. (Royal Philips Electronics, commonly known as Philips) is a Dutch multinational electronics company headquartered in Amsterdam. It was founded in Eindhoven in 1891 by Gerard Philips and his father Frederik. It is one of the largest electronics companies in the world and employs around 122,000 people across more than 60 countries.

Generally, plastic is best avoided in coffee making equipment, particularly for components that touch hot water. While BPA is widely recognized as a health concern when consumed in significant amounts, other chemical compounds used in plastic production can present greater risks, though they are less familiar to the public. Heat can accelerate the transfer of these substances from the plastic into the beverage, a process known as leaching. For this reason, materials like stainless steel, glass, or certified ceramics are often recommended for hot brewing stages to ensure purity and safety.

A plunger, or French press, is a manual brewing device featuring a cylindrical carafe and a plunger equipped with a metal mesh filter. Coffee grounds steep in hot water, and the plunger separates them to produce a full-bodied brew. This immersion method extracts rich flavors and retains natural oils, unlike paper-filtered methods, through direct contact between water and coffee.

A pod coffee machine brews single servings using pre-portioned, sealed capsules of ground coffee, delivering speed and consistency in every cup. Pioneered in the 1980s by brands like Nespresso and Keurig, these systems transformed home brewing by replacing manual measurements with unmatched convenience. The airtight pods keep coffee fresh while ensuring uniform extraction, though some purists critique the lack of customization.

Polycarbonate is a high-performance thermoplastic polymer known for its strength, clarity, and heat resistance Wikipedia . In coffee gear, it is valued for its thermal insulation, which is known for trapping heat up to 60% better than glass Acme Plastics . Its softening temperature can range from 150–160°C, while its glass transition temperature is approximately 145–150°C, ensuring durability and clarity at typical coffee-serving temperatures Merriam-Webster . Polycarbonate’s lightweight and impact-resistant properties make it ideal for travel mugs, French presses, and other coffee accessories. Its transparency is similar to glass, while its resistance to thermal stress plays a role in preventing cracks under rapid temperature changes, making it a reliable choice for both hot and cold beverages.

Porcelain is a preferred material for many coffee-making items, such as mugs , cups, drippers, kettles, and pots. Its widespread use comes from its unique qualities, which result from a special recipe and a precise making process. Although it is part of the larger ceramic family, porcelain is often seen as a premium choice. It can replace other ceramics for numerous tasks because it is more durable and has a finer, more elegant look.

Postum is a powdered roasted grain beverage often used as a coffee substitute . The caffeine-free beverage was created by Post Cereal Company founder C. W. Post in 1895 and marketed as a healthful alternative to coffee. (The Postum Cereal Company eventually became General Foods, which was bought by Kraft Foods. ) Post was a student of John Harvey Kellogg, who believed caffeine to be unhealthy. The “instant” drink mix version was developed in 1912, replacing the original brewed beverage.

Pour over coffee is a manual brewing method where hot water is poured over coffee grounds in a filter, allowing the brewed coffee to drip into a vessel below. The technique uses a controlled, circular pouring motion to ensure even extraction of flavors. It uses a grind size ranging from medium to fine, which is finer than French press but coarser than espresso, influencing extraction rate and flow.

Pre-infusion is the initial phase of espresso extraction where water is gently introduced to the coffee puck at low pressure (typically 1-3 bars) before full brewing pressure is applied. This technique, rooted in traditional lever espresso machines, serves two critical functions: it evenly hydrates the coffee grounds, allowing them to expand and release trapped gases, while simultaneously preventing channeling by eliminating dry pockets.

Pressure is the ratio of force to the area over which that force is distributed. Pressure is force per unit area applied in a direction perpendicular to the surface of an object. Gauge pressure (also spelled gage pressure) is the pressure relative to the local atmospheric or ambient pressure. While pressure may be measured in any unit of force divided by any unit of area, the SI unit of pressure is called the pascal (Pa) after the seventeenth-century philosopher and scientist Blaise Pascal.

Pressure profiling involves the controlled variation of water pressure during espresso extraction, adjusted in real time by the barista or programmed into an espresso machine. Unlike traditional espresso brewing, which has a steady pressure of around 9 bars, this technique enables precise manipulation of the extraction process, influencing variables like flow rate and contact time.

A pressure gauge is an instrument on an espresso machine that measures the water pressure applied to the coffee puck during extraction, typically displayed in bars or PSI (pounds per square inch). It ensures consistent espresso quality by monitoring the ideal 9-bar range, the standard for optimal extraction, preventing under-extraction or over-extraction.

A pressurized basket is a specialized portafilter basket designed to create artificial pressure during espresso extraction through a single, restricted exit hole. Unlike traditional baskets, it works with inconsistent grind size or uneven tamping by forcing water through this narrow opening, producing a crema-like foam. This adaptable design suits entry-level machines and beginners but limits extraction control, yielding less nuanced flavors than non-pressurized alternatives.

Coffee perception centers around five primary taste sensations detected by taste buds on the tongue and palate. Bitterness , the most prominent taste in coffee, results from compounds like caffeine and chlorogenic acids, with intensity varying based on roast level . Sweetness manifests as pleasant, sugar-like notes often found in properly extracted coffees. Sourness ( acidity ) contributes brightness and vibrancy, ranging from crisp citrus to softer malic acid notes.

Puckpuck is a specialized cold drip brewing attachment that converts an AeroPress into a slow-drip cold brew device. It consists of a drip regulator and a stand, enabling precise control over water flow for consistent extraction. By adjusting the drip rate, users can produce a clean, concentrated cold brew with balanced acidity and nuanced flavors, typically over several hours. The attachment’s compact design leverages the AeroPress’s portability, making it a practical option for home brewers seeking café-quality cold brew without bulky equipment. Cold drip brewing minimizes bitterness and astringency by avoiding prolonged immersion, resulting in a smoother, more aromatic cup. The Puckpuck’s affordability and simplicity have made it popular among coffee enthusiasts exploring alternative cold brew methods beyond traditional immersion or toddy systems.

Quakers are defective coffee beans that create distinct negative sensory characteristics when present in sufficient quantities within a coffee blend. These underdeveloped beans appear lighter in color compared to properly developed coffee beans , often displaying a pale, whitish, or lighter brown appearance that makes them identifiable during visual inspection. The flavor impact of quakers has harsh , astringent, and unpleasantly bitter notes that can overpower the desired flavor characteristics of quality coffee.

Rancid Flavor in Coffee: Definition and Sensory Profile Rancid flavor is a distinct off-note in coffee characterized by unpleasant, fatty, sour qualities reminiscent of spoiled butter or oxidized oils. In sensory evaluation, rancid notes present as a combination of stale, cardboard-like aromas with sour, pungent undertones. The flavor typically intensifies over time as coffee ages, particularly when stored improperly. Research comparing Arabica and Robusta varieties found that both develop rancid characteristics during storage, though at different rates .

Rancilio is an espresso machine manufacturer, founded in 1927 by Roberto Rancilio in Parabiago, Milan, Italy. Rancilio would become best known for its innovative distribution networks, effective use of industrial design and reputable reliability. Rancilio’s earliest well-known machine was ‘La Regina’ – a vertical boiler machine, similar to the original Bezzera and Victoria Arduino devices in function and gilded ‘Belle Epoque’ styling.

The Rancilio Silvia, introduced in 1997 by Italian manufacturer Rancilio, is a semi-automatic espresso machine designed for home use. Featuring commercial-grade components like a brass boiler and sturdy portafilter, it produces café-quality espresso when paired with proper technique and a high-quality grinder. Its durable construction and minimalist design appeal to espresso enthusiasts seeking skill development.

Ready To Drink Coffee (RTD) refers to pre-brewed, packaged coffee beverages made for immediate consumption without extra preparation. These products include cold brews, lattes, nitro coffees, and espresso shots, usually sold in cans, bottles, or cartons. RTD coffee gained popularity in Japan during the 1960s with canned coffee vending machines, later spreading globally as a convenient alternative to freshly brewed coffee. Its appeal lies in portability, consistency, and shelf stability, catering to busy consumers who prioritize speed without compromising quality.

A Red Eye is a coffee beverage that combines drip coffee with a shot of espresso. The standard preparation involves brewing an 8 oz (237 ml) cup of drip coffee using gravity filtration , then adding a 1 oz (30 ml) espresso shot produced under high pressure . This combination gives a significant caffeine boost, typically containing between 160-200 mg of caffeine, though exact amounts vary based on brew strength and shot size .

A review is an evaluation of a publication, product, service, or company such as a movie, video game, musical composition (music review of a composition or recording), book; a piece of hardware like a car, home appliance , or computer; or an event or performance, such as a live music concert, play, musical theater show, or dance show. In addition to a critical evaluation, the review’s author may assign the work a rating to indicate its relative merit.
A ristretto is a short, restricted espresso shot brewed with the same amount of coffee but half the water, producing a sweeter, more concentrated, and less bitter result.

Robusta coffee, also known as Coffea canephora or Coffea robusta, is a variety of coffee plant, with its origins in central and western sub-Saharan Africa. It is a species of flowering plant in the Rubiaceae family. Though widely known as Coffea robusta, the plant is scientifically identified as Coffea canephora, which has two main varieties – Robusta and Nganda.

Rubbery Flavor in Coffee: Definition and Sensory Profile Rubbery flavor is an undesirable taste characteristic in coffee that resembles burnt rubber or synthetic materials . This off-flavor indicates quality issues or processing problems in the coffee supply chain. When present, the rubbery notes create an unpleasant sensory experience that masks the coffee’s intended flavor profile.

The Specialty Coffee Association of America (SCAA), founded in 1982, is a non-profit trade organization for the specialty coffee industry. With members located in more than 40 countries, SCAA represents every segment of the specialty coffee industry, including producers, coffee roasters , importers/exporters, retailers,coffee brewing equipment manufacturers, baristas and other industry professionals.

Saeco International Group S.p.A., or Saeco for short, is an Italian manufacturer of manual, super-automatic and capsule based espresso machines as well other electrical goods, with headquarters and factories in Gaggio Montano, located near Bologna.

Scorched coffee represents one of the most recognizable roasting defects, occurring when excessive heat application damages coffee beans during the roasting process. This defect shows when roasters apply too much heat quickly, particularly during the early stages, causing the bean’s exterior to burn while the interior remains underdeveloped . The resulting coffee has characteristic burnt, acrid flavors that overpower the bean’s natural characteristics. The phenomenon differs from intentionally dark roasts through its uneven development pattern.

A screen filter is a type of filter using a rigid or flexible screen to separate sand and other fine particles out of water. Typical screen materials include stainless steel , polypropylene, nylon and polyester.

Semi-automatic espresso machines are devices that partially automate the espresso brewing process . Compared with super automatic machines , they require more work and know-how from the barista. They are the choice of coffee shops and espresso aficionados. They offer excellent reliability and control over the brewing process.

Senseo is a registered trademark for a coffee brewing system from Dutch companies Philips and Douwe Egberts. The three main characteristics of the system are its coffee pods (called pads in some countries), its design and its easy to use system.

Single in the context of espresso brewing , refers to a single shot of espresso , pulled from approximately 7-8 grams of coffee grounds. Also called a solo, by the Italian name, a single shot normale espresso holds about 1 oz. of brewed coffee, and it is prepared using a single filter basket .
Single origin coffee comes from one specific geographic location (country, region, or farm), allowing the unique terroir and flavor characteristics of that place to be expressed.

Single-origin coffee is coffee grown within a single known geographical origin. Sometimes this is a single farm or a specific collection of beans from a single country. The name of the coffee is then usually the place it was grown to whatever degree available. Single-origins are viewed by some as a way to get a specific taste, and some independent coffee shops have found that this gives them a way to add value over large chains.

A siphon brewer is a vacuum-style coffee maker that uses vapor pressure and gravity to cycle water between two chambers—first steeping coffee grounds, then filtering the brewed coffee downward. Developed in the 1830s, this hybrid immersion-and-filtration method achieves precise temperature control , yielding a sediment-free cup with exceptional clarity and aroma.

Small appliances, also called brown goods (because the color of the wooden and bakelite cases once used) are portable or semi-portable machines, generally used on table-tops, counter-tops, or other platforms, to accomplish a household task. Examples of brown goods are: television and wireless sets; microwave ovens; coffee makers; and personal computers.

Smoothness in coffee represents a harmonious sensory experience characterized by a low-acidity, mellow flavor profile that lacks harshness or bitterness . This quality shows a pleasant mouthfeel—neither thin nor watery—that glides across the palate without astringency . The perception of smoothness emerges when all flavor components integrate seamlessly, with no single element creating jarring sensations. Achieving this balance requires proper brewing conditions, particularly water quality and temperature. Filtered water heated to 195–205°F (90–96°C) helps produce consistently smooth results.

SOLVENT In coffee chemistry, a solvent is a substance that dissolves other materials (solutes) during brewing. Water serves as the primary solvent in coffee preparation , extracting hundreds of compounds that contribute to flavor, aroma, and mouthfeel . The solvent’s effectiveness depends on temperature , contact time , and pressure. In decaffeination processes, various solvents play crucial roles: water alone (Swiss Water Process), supercritical carbon dioxide, ethyl acetate, or methylene chloride. .

Sourness in coffee refers to a bright, sharp, tangy, or tart taste sensation, primarily perceived on the sides of the tongue, and is a fundamental taste attribute distinct from bitterness. This characteristic is central in coffee evaluation. When balanced and pleasant, it is described as “ acidity ” or “ brightness ,” which plays a role in a coffee’s complexity and liveliness.

South America, earlier known simply as America (1507–1538), is a continent located in the Western Hemisphere, mostly in the Southern Hemisphere, with a relatively small portion in the Northern Hemisphere. It is also considered a subcontinent of the Americas. It is bordered on the west by the Pacific Ocean and on the north and east by the Atlantic Ocean; North America and the Caribbean Sea lie to the northwest.
Specialty coffee refers to coffee that scores 80 or above on the SCA 100-point scale, representing the highest quality tier with traceable origins and exceptional flavor.

Spicy notes in coffee represent a diverse category of aromatic and flavor characteristics that add complexity to the cup. On the Specialty Coffee Association ( Specialty Coffee Association (SCA)) Flavor Wheel, spice descriptors appear in multiple sections, including the brown spice family (cinnamon, clove, nutmeg) and pungent spices (black pepper, anise) .

In metallurgy, stainless steel , also known as inox steel or inox from French “inoxydable”, is a steel alloy with a minimum of 10.5% to 11% chromium content by mass. Stainless steel does not readily corrode, rust or stain with water as ordinary steel does, but despite the name it is not fully stain-proof, most notably under low oxygen, high salinity, or poor circulation environments.

Starbucks Corporation is an American global coffee company and coffee house chain based in Seattle, Washington. Starbucks is the largest coffeehouse company in the world, with 20,891 stores in 62 countries, including 13,279 in the United States, 1,324 in Canada, 989 in Japan, 851 in China, 806 in the United Kingdom, 556 in South Korea, 377 in Mexico, 291 in Taiwan, 206 in the Philippines, 171 in Thailand and 10 in India.
Although steam is generally too hot for brewing coffee, the power of steam is used in certain coffee brewing methods to create pressure . Pressure, in turn, improves the extraction .
A steam wand is a metal tube on an espresso machine that injects steam into milk to heat and froth it for lattes, cappuccinos, and other milk-based drinks.

Steamed milk—heated and aerated by an espresso machine ‘s steam wand —has a velvety microfoam with subtle sweetness. The steam heats the milk while forming tiny air bubbles, yielding a smooth texture. Essential for espresso drinks like lattes and cappuccinos, steamed milk softens the espresso’s intensity while adding body and richness. Maintaining the ideal temperature range (140–160°F) preserves milk’s natural sugars without scalding, enhancing specialty coffee . For baristas, mastering this technique is critical—it uses the foundation of crafting balanced coffee drinks.

A Steampunk Coffeemaker is a commercial single-cup brewer that harnesses halogen heating, vacuum pressure, and digital precision to recreate siphon-style extraction. Developed by Alpha Dominche in the early 2010s, this innovative system enables baristas to fine-tune water temperature and agitation with surgical accuracy, yielding a remarkably clean and nuanced cup.

Steeping time—the period coffee grounds soak in water during immersion brewing —is a pivotal variable controlling flavor extraction. It directly governs how much oils, soluble compounds, and aromatic elements dissolve, shaping the brew’s taste, strength, and mouthfeel. Extended steeping increases extraction for bolder intensity, while shorter durations highlight brighter, nuanced flavors.

The stomach is a muscular, hollow, dilated part of the digestion system which functions as an important organ of the digestive tract in some animals, including vertebrates, echinoderms, insects (mid-gut), and molluscs. It is involved in the second phase of digestion, following mastication (chewing). The stomach is located between the esophagus and the small intestine.

An electric stove or electric range is a stove that converts electrical energy into heat to cook and bake. Stoves are used for coffee preparation in order to heat up water. There are many manual brewing methods that require hot water, but they don’t involve an automated way to do it.

A super-automatic espresso machine performs all or almost all of the coffee brewing automatically. A super automatic espresso machine will automate the following operations that are typically performed manually by the barista:
Surface area is the measurement of the total area (faces or curved surface) of a solid figure.

Taint (pronounced /teɪnt/) is a specific quality defect in coffee, defined as a noticeable but not overwhelming undesirable off- flavor or aroma that falls outside the expected profile. It is a category of sensory defect less severe than a “fault,” which would make the coffee unpalatable. The term is standardized in professional cupping protocols, such as those from the Specialty Coffee Association (SCA), to describe aromatic off-flavors that are perceptible but not overpowering.

Takeya, a Japanese brand renowned for its cold brew coffee makers, focuses on its signature airtight pitcher featuring a fine-mesh infuser for steeping coarsely ground coffee in cold water. Designed for home use, the pitcher’s BPA-free Tritan construction and leak-proof seal streamline the process of creating smooth , low-acid cold brew over 12 to 24 hours.

The Tassimo Hot Beverage System is a consumer coffee machine that prepares one-cup servings of espresso, regular coffee, tea, hot chocolate , and various other coffee drinks, notably those including milk such as latte or cappuccino . It was first introduced in France in 2004 and is now also available in Andorra, Austria, Canada, Czech Republic, Greece, Germany, Norway, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Russia, Poland, Portugal, the United Kingdom and the United States.

Taste, gustatory perception, or gustation is one of the five traditional senses. Taste is the sensation produced when a substance in the mouth reacts chemically with receptors of taste buds. Taste, along with smell and trigeminal nerve stimulation (which also handles touch for texture, also pain, and temperature), determines flavors, the sensory impressions of food or other substances.

Technivorm is a Dutch coffeemaker manufacturer. Technivorm manufactures the Moccamaster, one of the few coffee makers approved by the SCAA . They also manufacture coffee grinders , but they are most known for their flagship product the Moccamaster.

Temperature surfing is a manual technique used to stabilize brew temperature on home espresso machines with cycling thermostats. This method involves timing extraction to coincide with a specific phase in the heating cycle, addressing temperature fluctuations common in lower-cost machines like the Rancilio Silvia. Precise temperature control is critical for even extraction and balanced flavor.

Temperature control is a process in which change of temperature of a space (and objects collectively there within) is measured or otherwise detected, and the passage of heat energy into or out of the space is adjusted to achieve a desired average temperature.
Terroir refers to the environmental factors (altitude, soil, climate, rainfall) of a coffee growing region that impart distinctive flavor characteristics to the beans.

Glassware in coffee brewing equipment is exposed to thermal shock when hot water, or coffee is poured into glass beakers, carafes, or other recipients. In order to solve the problem with glass cracking, manufacturers use borosilicate glass , which is resistant to thermal shocks.

A thermoblock is a compact, on-demand heating element in espresso machines, where water flows through internal channels of a heated metal block—typically aluminum or stainless steel . Unlike traditional boilers, thermoblocks heat water instantly during flow, eliminating warm-up delays and reducing energy consumption. This efficiency enables smaller, cost-effective machines, fueling their dominance in home espresso setups.

A thermocoil is a heating system in espresso machines where water flows through a coiled metal tube heated by an internal electric element. Unlike traditional boilers that store and heat larger water volumes, it heats water on demand, reducing warm-up time while maintaining precise temperature control. This design enhances energy efficiency and minimizes temperature fluctuations, crucial for balanced espresso flavor.
The thermostat is a key component of coffee brewing equipment. It is used to ensure coffee is brewed properly, and the extraction is optimal.

Timers are used in coffee makers for various applications. The most common applications are: timing the brewing , starting the coffee maker, or turning it off, timing coffee grinders, as a way to measure the amount of coffee beans used, timing the extraction as a way of controlling the brewed coffee volume.

Tobacco notes in coffee describe a complex flavor profile in the brew, characterized by earthy, woody, and somewhat smoky characteristics that resemble the aroma of dried tobacco leaves. These notes typically present as dry, leathery sensations on the palate, often in darker roasts, accompanied by subtle hints of cedar or hay. The flavor shows most prominently in the coffee’s finish, leaving a lingering impression similar to the scent of a tobacco pouch after extraction .

Toddy is a cold brew coffee concentrate created by steeping coarse coffee grounds in cold water for 12–24 hours using the Toddy® immersion system, developed by Todd Simpson in the 1960s. This slow extraction yields a smooth, low-acid concentrate with minimal bitterness , ideal for mixing with water or milk or as a base for other drinks.

Total Dissolved Solids (often abbreviated TDS) is a measure of the combined content of all inorganic and organic substances contained in a liquid in: molecular, ionized or micro-granular suspended form. Generally the operational definition is that the solids must be small enough to survive filtration through a sieve the size of two micrometer. Total dissolved solids are normally discussed only for freshwater systems, as salinity comprises some of the ions constituting the definition of TDS.

Triple, in the context of espresso brewing , refers to a triple shot of espresso, pulled from approximately 21 grams of coffee grounds. The triple is pulled using special filter baskets that can hold the necessary 21 grams of coffee. Triplo, as is also called with the Italian name, is not just simply a time and volume adjustment variant of the solo. The triple shot needs to be pulled in about the same time as a single. For this, the grind size needs to be adjusted accordingly.
Turkish coffee is an unfiltered brewing method where very finely ground coffee is simmered in water in a small pot called a cezve, producing a thick, strong, and aromatic beverage.

In the coffee maker industry there are many devices that are equipped with a valve. The use of a valve is different though from a coffee brewing method to another. Immersion coffee makers such as coffee drippers, use a valve to control the steeping time . A simple valve is often found on automatic drip coffee machines as a way to temporarily stop the dripping for pouring a cup.

Vibration refers to a mechanical phenomenon involving oscillations about an equilibrium point. The motion is calibrated by frequency and amplitude to match specific bean size profiles, enabling processes such as specific gravity separation and density-based bean separation.
A Vienna roast is a medium-dark roast level, darker than an American roast but lighter than Full City or French roast.

Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê đá) is a distinctive cold coffee beverage characterized by its bold flavor profile and layered presentation. This drink typically consists of strong, dark-roasted coffee—traditionally made with robusta beans —combined with sweetened condensed milk and poured over ice. Visually, Vietnamese iced coffee presents as a striking two-toned beverage when unmixed, with the thick white condensed milk layer beneath the dark coffee. Once stirred, it transforms into a caramel-colored drink.

In chemistry and physics, volatility is the tendency of a substance to vaporize. Volatility is directly related to a substance’s vapor pressure. At a given temperature, a substance with higher vapor pressure vaporizes more readily than a substance with a lower vapor pressure.

Many coffee makers rely on a water tank, or reservoir to supply the machine during brewing. The water tank solution is convenient, makes it possible to move the equipment, and it doesn’t require an expensive installation.

Wiener Melange (pronounced VEE-ner meh-LAHNJ, from German for “ Viennese blend”) refers to a traditional Austrian coffee beverage . It is a gentler, creamier variation of a cappuccino , distinguished by its use of milder coffee and a balanced ratio of coffee to milk . The drink consists of a shot of espresso or lightly brewed coffee, an equal amount of steamed milk, and is topped with a light milk foam .

Developed in 1954 by German inventor Gottlob Widmann, the Wigomat revolutionized home brewing as the first fully automatic drip coffee maker. Its design featured an electric heating element, paper filter, and automated drip mechanism, replacing manual pour-over methods while ensuring consistent temperature and extraction for balanced flavor.

Winey Coffee refers to coffee with distinct wine-like characteristics in its flavor profile. This descriptor indicates a cup with bright acidity , fruity notes , and a complex, sometimes fermented quality that resembles wine . The sensory experience includes berry-like flavors (blackberry, blueberry), red fruits (cherry, currant), and occasionally dark grape notes . This profile commonly appears in coffees processed using natural or honey methods, where controlled fermentation develops these distinctive attributes .

Woody Coffee refers to a flavor and aroma characteristic in coffee that is reminiscent of dry wood, oak barrels, or tree bark. This descriptor is complex and can range from a valued note in some premium coffees to an undesirable defect. The distinction depends on whether the woody note is a fresh, intrinsic part of the flavor profile or a stale one resulting from improper storage or excessive aging.

The word “coffee” traces its roots to the Arabic “qahwah,” which originally referred to wine but later became associated with the beverage made from coffee beans . This term evolved as it traveled through trade routes, becoming “kahve” in Turkish and eventually “coffee” in English by the 16th century.

A coffee bean refers to the dried and roasted seed of a tropical plant belonging to the genus * Coffea * . Botanically, it is not a true bean but the pit found inside the coffee cherry fruit. The plural form is “coffee beans” .
Grind size is an important factor in coffee preparation, and it refers to the how fine or coarse the coffee bean is ground in order to prepare the coffee beverage.
A coffee grinder is a device for crushing coffee beans into fine grains or a powder. There are several types of coffee grinders, the most popular ones are burr grinders and blade grinders.

A coffee roasting company, or a coffee roaster for short, is a company that buys green coffee beans and roasts them. A coffee roaster sells various single origin or blends of coffee beans . There are various types of roasteries, depending on the niche and the company size. The third wave of coffee brought to the consumer’s attention micro roasters and artisan roasters, who cater to specialty coffee consumers and roast in small batches.

Roasting, in general, is a cooking method that uses dry heat, whether an open flame, oven, or other heat source. Roasting can enhance flavor through caramelization and Maillard browning on the surface of the food.

A coffee substitute is a substance that is consumed instead of coffee . It will normally have coffee like properties such as taste and appearance. Coffee drinkers will often drink coffee substitutes if they are trying to avoid coffee but want to have the coffee experience.
Crema is the golden-brown, foam-like layer that forms on top of a freshly pulled espresso shot, composed of emulsified coffee oils and CO2 bubbles.
Coffee brewing requires following strict recipes. This includes brewing temperature, coffee grind size , brewing time and the coffee dose.

Filter Basket: Definition and Core Function A filter basket is a perforated metal component that fits inside an espresso machine ‘s portafilter, designed to hold ground coffee during the brewing process . It has tiny holes through which pressurized hot water passes, extracting flavor compounds from the coffee grounds. Filter baskets come in various sizes, with 18g capacity being recommended for consistent home brewing . While 8g baskets exist for single shots, they present extraction challenges .
A portafilter is the handle-equipped filter basket that holds ground coffee in an espresso machine, locking into the group head for pressurized extraction.

A single serve coffee maker is a coffeemaker that can be used to brew a single cup of coffee. The concept of single serve is usually related to automatic drip coffee brewers, since the classic automatic drip coffee machine cannot make small quantities of coffee. Although espresso machines brew a single serve, they are not included in the category. The same with manual coffee brewers.
A tamper is a flat-bottomed tool used to compress ground coffee evenly in an espresso portafilter basket, creating a uniform puck for consistent extraction.

Bolivia is a coffee-producing country in west-central South America , a small but distinctive origin whose farms sit among the highest coffee-growing elevations on earth. Its coffee industry is modest by volume yet increasingly valued by specialty buyers for clean , sweet, floral lots that are hard to find elsewhere.

Brazil is the world’s largest coffee-producing country, supplying roughly a third of all coffee grown on earth, and a defining coffee origin in its own right. A South American giant whose output dwarfs every other origin, Brazil anchors the global market and provides the base of countless espresso blends thanks to its smooth, low-acid, chocolatey profile.

Burundi is a small, landlocked coffee-producing country in East Africa’s Great Lakes region and a rising specialty origin. Despite its size, it has earned a strong specialty reputation for bright, sweet, berry-driven coffees grown by hundreds of thousands of smallholder families at high elevations.

China is a rising coffee-producing country, with nearly all of its Arabica grown in the southern province of Yunnan. A relatively new player on the global origin map, China has expanded planting rapidly and is increasingly exporting clean , mild, approachable coffees.

Colombia is one of the world’s leading coffee-producing countries and the most famous Arabica origin in the Americas. Its washed, high-grown coffees are the benchmark for balance, prized worldwide for a smooth, caramel-sweet cup with a bright, clean finish.

Costa Rica is a Central American coffee-producing country with an outsized reputation for quality and one of the defining origins of the specialty era. Though small in volume, it was the first country to ban Robusta by law and pioneered the honey process, producing clean, bright, sweet coffees that helped define specialty coffee.

Cuba is a Caribbean coffee-producing country and coffee origin with a long growing tradition centred on the Sierra Maestra mountains. Its small Arabica harvest is known for a smooth, mild, low-acid cup, and its coffee culture produced the intensely sweet cafecito served across the island.

The Dominican Republic is a Caribbean coffee-producing country and coffee origin on the island of Hispaniola, with most of its Arabica grown in the highlands of the Barahona region. Its coffees are mild, sweet, and balanced, with a smooth body typical of well-made island coffee.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo is a large coffee-producing country in Central Africa and a resurgent coffee origin, with its best Arabica grown on the shores of Lake Kivu. Its high-grown coffees are full-bodied and deeply fruity, and its speciality sector has rebuilt after decades of conflict.

Ecuador is a coffee-producing country on South America’s Pacific coast and a small but fast-rising coffee origin, stretching from Andean highlands down to the Galápagos. Its high-grown Arabica from the southern province of Loja is increasingly celebrated for a sweet, floral, complex cup.

El Salvador is a small Central American coffee-producing country and a respected coffee origin with a long and proud growing heritage. Its highland farms produce sweet, honeyed, chocolate-toned coffees, and the country is famous for the Pacamara variety it helped bring to the world stage.

Guatemala is a Central American coffee-producing country renowned for some of the region’s most distinctive, full-bodied coffees, and one of its premier coffee origins. Its volcanic highlands — above all the Antigua valley — yield cups with rich chocolate, gentle smoke, and a bright, complex finish.

Honduras is the largest coffee-producing country in Central America by volume and a rising force in specialty coffee . Its highland farms turn out sweet, balanced, nutty -and- caramel coffees that have quietly become a mainstay of blends and single origins alike.

India is a major coffee-producing country in South Asia and the origin of the famous Monsooned Malabar process. Its southern plantations grow both Arabica and Robusta , yielding smooth , low-acid coffees that underpin the country’s beloved filter-coffee tradition.

Indonesia is one of the world’s largest coffee-producing countries and the source of some of its most distinctive beans, a coffee origin defined by its island terroir. Its coffees — from Sumatra, Java, and Sulawesi — are famous for a heavy, earthy, low-acid cup shaped by the unique wet-hulled process.

Jamaica is a Caribbean coffee-producing country best known for its Blue Mountain coffee, one of the most famous and expensive coffees in the world, and a coffee origin synonymous with luxury. Grown in a strictly defined highland zone, it is prized for a mild, sweet, impeccably balanced cup.

Kenya is an East African coffee-producing country whose coffees are among the most distinctive and sought-after in the world, and one of the great benchmark origins. Known for intense blackcurrant and berry notes and a wine-like acidity, Kenyan coffee sets the standard for bright, complex African flavour.

Laos is a landlocked coffee-producing country in Southeast Asia and an emerging coffee origin, with most of its crop grown on the volcanic Bolaven Plateau in the south. Its Arabica is sweet and mild, and its coffee sector has grown steadily as a source of rural income.

Malawi is a small East African coffee-producing country and an emerging coffee origin whose highland Arabica is a rising specialty name. Grown mainly in the northern Mzuzu region, Malawian coffee is sweet, floral, and bright, with a clean finish that belies the country’s small output.

Mexico is one of the world’s larger coffee-producing countries, with a long growing tradition across its southern states, and a longstanding coffee origin. Its highland Arabica is mild and smooth, with nutty, chocolate notes, and much of it is shade-grown and organic.

Myanmar is an emerging coffee-producing country in Southeast Asia and a young coffee origin, with its best Arabica grown in the cool highlands of Shan State. Its coffees are sweet and fruity, and its specialty sector has grown rapidly as a source of rural development.

Nicaragua is a Central American coffee-producing country and a dependable coffee origin, whose highland coffees are sweet, balanced, and chocolatey. Grown across the northern highlands around Jinotega and Matagalpa, Nicaraguan coffee is a crowd-pleasing favourite.

Panama is a small coffee-producing country that has become legendary in specialty coffee as the home of the Geisha variety, and one of the world’s most coveted coffee origins. Grown on the volcanic slopes of Boquete and Volcán, Panamanian Geisha commands record prices for its astonishing floral, tea-like cup.

Papua New Guinea is a coffee-producing country in the western Pacific and a distinctive coffee origin whose highland Arabica grows in remote, rugged terrain. Its coffees are sweet and full-bodied, with a syrupy texture and a fruity, gently earthy character.

Peru is a leading coffee-producing country on the eastern slopes of the Andes and a major coffee origin known for high-grown, organic Arabica. Its coffees are mild and sweet, with nutty, chocolate notes and a clean finish, grown largely by smallholder farmers.

Puerto Rico is a Caribbean coffee-producing island and coffee origin with a heritage dating back centuries. Its highland Arabica is smooth, sweet, and balanced, and the island’s coffee tradition is celebrated in its daily café culture.

Rwanda, the “land of a thousand hills,” is a small East African coffee-producing country and a model specialty origin, whose Bourbon coffees are bright, floral, and sweet. Its sector has become a benchmark of quality-driven, smallholder-led production.

Tanzania is an East African coffee-producing country whose coffees grow on the slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro and the southern highlands. Known for bright , fruity , sweet cups — and for its prized peaberry lots — Tanzania is a respected origin in its own right.

Thailand is a coffee-producing country in Southeast Asia and a growing coffee origin, with most of its Arabica grown in the northern highlands around Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai. Its coffees are mild, sweet, and increasingly refined, alongside a strong domestic coffee-drinking culture.

Uganda is a major coffee-producing country in East Africa and one of the world’s leading Robusta growers, and a substantial coffee origin. Its highland Arabica from Mount Elgon and the Rwenzori range is full-bodied and winey, while its Robusta anchors blends worldwide.

Vietnam is the world’s second-largest coffee-producing country and its leading Robusta grower, and a powerhouse coffee origin. Its coffee, centred on the Central Highlands, is bold, earthy, and heavy-bodied, powering espresso blends, instant coffee, and the country’s famous sweetened iced coffee.

Yemen is a historic coffee-producing country and the birthplace of the world coffee trade, the source of the legendary Mocha and one of the oldest coffee origins on earth. Its highland Arabica, dried naturally on sun-baked terraces, is prized for a wild, winey, spiced cup unlike any other origin.
Bourbon is a classic Arabica coffee variety known for its sweetness, balanced acidity, and complex flavor profile, originally cultivated on the island of Reunion (formerly Bourbon).
Typica is one of the oldest and most genetically important Arabica coffee varieties, serving as the parent of many modern cultivars and known for its clean, sweet cup quality.
Caturra is a natural mutation of Bourbon with a compact plant size, higher yield, and bright, citrusy flavor profile, widely grown in Central and South America.
Catimor is a hybrid variety created by crossing Caturra with Timor Hybrid, offering disease resistance to coffee leaf rust while maintaining reasonable cup quality.
Catuai is a hybrid Arabica variety developed in Brazil by crossing Caturra and Mundo Novo, known for its compact size, high yield, and resistance to wind and rain.
Geisha (or Gesha) is a rare, highly prized Arabica variety from Ethiopia, celebrated for its extraordinary floral, jasmine, and bergamot flavor notes and exceptional cup quality.
